cards.title: Memory/allocation controls push: arenas, ref fields, uninit, buffers, opt-in GC
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 memory/allocation push. Merges explicit allocation boundaries (#119), visible uninit (#83), opt-in GC (#69), and labeled ref fields (#147) into the arena/allocation inference track. This card owns expert-tier memory controls while preserving safe beginner defaults.
cards.plan:
Canonical memory/allocation implementation plan. Preserve I1: beginner Jet stays safe; expert controls require explicit syntax/imports/audit where applicable.

Build order:
1. Labeled stored references: implement #Ref(Label) field syntax and owner relationship checks; remove stale core.mem gate per owner outcome; migrate old ref[label] diagnostics.
2. Arena allocator inference: keep current arena plan as base; prove region views cannot escape, reset/free invalidates views, and diagnostics remain Jet-owned.
3. Explicit allocation boundaries: audit Core APIs that allocate across caller-owned boundaries; add buffer/allocator-taking variants using existing allocator model; add lint for hidden boundary allocation in expert/perf contexts.
4. Visible uninit: #Uninit binding, explicit type/no initializer parser rules, definite-assignment proof, plain-data restriction, MaybeUninit codegen only after sema proof; E0421-E0424 snapshots.
5. Opt-in GC library: Gc<T> traced handle as library type for cyclic long-running data, explicit import, no default allocation path change, no sema/codegen primitive unless needed for root tracing.

Acceptance: ui snapshots for dangling/escaping refs, uninit misuse, arena use-after-reset, hidden allocation lint; examples for arena parsing, #Ref owner labels, caller buffers, #Uninit fixed buffers, cyclic Gc graph; golden tests; no generated unsafe outside #Unsafe/std-mem internals.

Codegen: TStmt::LineMarker + emit_bundle_dbg/compile_for_debug emit `// jet:line N` markers gated by cx.debug_linemap (off by default — zero effect on normal builds, golden tests, or the JIT tier; confirmed via full test suite + `cargo test --workspace` diffing). New Source/Debug/{LineMap,Inferior,Native,Dap}.rs. `jet debug` auto-dispatches interpreter vs native via the SAME E2203 boundary scan (needs_native) — one command, one meaning (I8); `--dap` forces native for editor launch; `--raw-frames` (D-DBG2) shows raw Rust file:line. Live-lldb verification surfaced and fixed THREE real bugs a docs-only implementation would have shipped broken: (1) lldb never re-prints a bare prompt over a pipe (echoes command instead) — naive prompt-wait hangs forever, fixed with a sentinel-command read loop; (2) a resume command's own stop banner is asynchronous and can lose a race to the NEXT command's reply — fixed by always deriving position from a synchronous follow-up `bt`, never the resume's own text; (3) the debuggee inherits lldb's stdout by default, so a Jet `print()` can tear a control-channel sentinel in half — fixed by redirecting debuggee stdout/stderr to temp files via `settings set target.output/error-path` and draining them into the transcript. Also loads rustc's own Rust pretty-printer (lldb_lookup.py + lldb_commands, same two files rust-lldb loads) so String/&str locals render as `"text"` instead of raw allocator internals. Tests: 12 new unit tests (LineMap/Inferior, no lldb needed) + tests/debug_native.rs (5 tests, gated on lldb presence like tests/observe.rs gates on rustc — skips clean without it). New example examples/features/189_debug_native.jet (native-only via `use core.fs`) + golden .out. cards.title: Full HTTP core library — client + server (D-NETDEP1=A, owner-expanded mandate)
cards.body: Owner mandate (2026-06-26, expanding D-NETDEP1=A): Jet ships a full, complete HTTP library — both client AND server — as a core library, better than Go's net/http. D-NETDEP1's approved pure-Rust crate (ureq/minreq) is only the BOOTSTRAP backing c157's build-time fetch(url, sha256:); the native-ize end-state (Epoch-3 dep rule) is a first-party Jet/Rust HTTP stdlib. SCOPE: client (request/response, methods, headers, body, streaming, TLS, redirects, timeouts) + server (listener, router, handler, middleware, request/response types, graceful shutdown). The client+server API surface (naming + shapes) is SYNTAX/stdlib-surface design needing its own decision docs + ballots BEFORE code — drive from a real-world example per owner-anti-repetition + owner-decision-doc-style. NOT this card: c157's fetch backend (ships first against the bootstrap crate).
cards.plan:
Full HTTP core library — client + server (D-NETDEP1=A mandate; D-HTTPLIB1=A function-first mux; D-HTTPLIB2=B split client/server; D-HTTPLIB3=C HTTP/1.1+HTTP/2+WebSocket; D-HTTPLIB4=B rustls TLS — all ratified & in canon). Bootstrap crates (ureq/hyper, tungstenite, rustls/webpki-roots) wired via the stdlib FFI-bridge pattern (emit bridge template text; never add to the jet compiler Cargo.toml; I6 holds — never in Source/). Native-ize end-state: first-party Jet/Rust HTTP stack.
Staged build: (1) core.http.client — Request/Response, methods, headers, body, streaming, redirects, timeouts, rustls TLS; this also provides the backend for c157's comptime `fetch(url, sha256:)` (record {url,sha256} in .jet/lock) — ship first to unblock c157. (2) core.http.server — listener, function-first `mux` (mux.get/post(path, fn(req:Request)->Response)), `req.params["id"]`, middleware, graceful shutdown. (3) HTTP/2 + WebSocket upgrade. Each stage: examples + goldens; no I4 diagnostics unless misuse surfaces. Big multi-PR track — sequence client before server.

cards.title: Static guarantees push: refinements, contracts, IFC, budgets, bounds, replay soundness
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 sema-proof/policy push. Merges information-flow (#24), budgets (#26), formal verification/contracts (#27), out-of-bounds proof escape (#106), and replay soundness (#23) into refinement types (#25). These features share one facts engine/call graph/policy infrastructure and must not grow separate proof systems.
cards.plan:
Canonical static-guarantees implementation plan. Build one sema facts/policy engine, then layer features on it. No duplicate proof engines.

Build order:
1. Facts core: represent refinements as named predicate-backed types; collect comparison/range/require facts; branch narrowing; loop facts; fixed-list length facts; call pre/postcondition facts.
2. Contracts: require/ensure syntax and runtime/test checks where ratified; jet test harvests contracts as property/property-test seeds; diagnostics point at the violated contract and caller path.
3. Bounds proof: default runtime bounds checks stay; elide or expert-escape only where facts prove in-range. Add explicit unsafe/proof escape only if ratified; no silent unchecked indexing.
4. Information-flow/compliance: security-label lattice as sema policy over values; declassify is explicit and audited; labels propagate through calls, collections, serialization, and task boundaries.
5. Budgets: #Budget/profile markers feed the same call graph/facts layer; enforce forbidden effects, bounded loops, and budget diagnostics without a second effect system.
6. Replay soundness: reuse effect/inverse-propagation walk; raise/attach D-REPLAY2 if marker spelling is still missing before parser work; reject reachable Time/Rand/Net/Io unless mockable under replay.
7. Solver/proof integration: formal proof hooks consume the same facts and contracts; generated obligations must report Jet diagnostics, never prover internals.

Acceptance: ui snapshots for missing refinement proof, failed contract, unsafe/unknown bounds proof, IFC leak, invalid declassify, budget violation, replay-unsound call path; examples/goldens for PositiveInt, safe index, PII declassify, render-frame budget, replayable pure handler, formal proof stub; docs/spec/diagnostics.md codes for each user-facing diagnostic.

cards.plan:
Canonical crypto/secrets implementation plan. Default API must be misuse-resistant; raw primitives stay expert-only.

Build order:
1. Preserve/finish RNG split prerequisite: deterministic PRNG and CSPRNG remain structurally separate.
2. Envelope API: crypto.seal/open and crypto.sign/verify hide nonce/mode/key details; versioned envelope metadata; clear error types; no raw AES/ChaCha/RSA beginner path.
3. Algorithm agility: design hybrid-ready envelope metadata and algorithm ids now; do not expose PQ primitive until backend exists; migration tests prove old envelopes still open.
4. TTL/rotting secrets: core.time.Expiring<T> and core.secrets.Rotting<T>; constructors require clock/context and deadline/ttl; access returns T? or fallible expired error.
5. Static/lint support: warn/error for expired unwrap in test-known clock cases; reject crypto API misuse that bypasses envelope surface.

Acceptance: examples for seal/open, sign/verify, envelope version migration, expiring cache, rotating secret; golden tests; ui snapshots for wrong RNG/raw primitive misuse/expired unchecked access; docs explain expert escape hatches.

log.text: 2026-07-09 truth audit: reclassified from shipped capability to historical substrate; world-class milestone owns live completion.

Independently re-verified with EXTRA scrutiny (orchestrator) given this card touches the core compile pipeline (I2/I3): nix develop -c cargo build --workspace clean. Targeted tests confirmed exactly: tests/build_cache_normalization.rs 10/10 (whitespace/comment/rename/reorder/profile/version-sensitive + 4 extra discrimination guards), tests/build_cache_race.rs 1/1 (8-concurrent-process integrity check), crates/jet-foundation lib CanonicalAST:: 3/3.

(2) edited the source (changed the printed string) and re-ran — correctly re-ran the full pipeline (front-end summary reappeared) and printed the NEW string, confirming edit/rename-sensitivity holds in practice. (3) jet build produced a working binary. (4) manually reproduced the exact race scenario from the plan: 3 concurrent jet run processes, all named main.jet in different directories with different content, launched simultaneously via nix develop's shell — each process's stdout correctly matched its own source with zero cross-contamination, confirming the cache-poisoning race fix holds under a real concurrent run, not just the automated 8-process regression test.

Full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace run to completion, exit code 0, zero FAILED/error lines. The I2/I3 soundness argument (cache hit = replay of a previously-validated exact whole-program AST + toolchain version + manifest bytes + profile, never a validation bypass; embed_file/embed_bytes correctly declines caching rather than risk external-state staleness) was reviewed and holds — no gap found on the orchestrator's independent read either. This was the last card in the owner's stated jetpack sequence for this session (#99 -> #176 -> #90 -> #3 -> #13 -> #179 -> #85). Closing: phase -> done.

E4 prep: plan expanded, zero ballots. Located real cache-poisoning race (CmdCompile.rs build(): rustc -o onto shared build/<stem> before store_cached copy — concurrent same-stem processes cross-contaminate) + fix (per-process temp path, atomic rename). D-BUILDNORM1=A ratified but cache_key hashes post-codegen Rust today, defeating incremental point — plan moves key to pre-sema canonical AST bytes + toolchain salt. Hash naming interlocked with #3 envelope.

Interlock noted 2026-07-02: D-JPK-CACHE1=A freezes cache-envelope fields (output hash, platform key, signature slot, provenance link) into the hangar/lock schema — normalization contract must carry them.

Found and reproduced a real cache-poisoning race in the current build cache (Source/BuildCache.rs + Source/CmdCompile.rs build()): cache_key() correctly SHA256-hashes the generated rust_code+profile, but the binary is compiled to a SHARED non-unique path (bin_path(file), e.g. build/main, keyed by source stem only) BEFORE store_cached(key, &bin) copies it into the content-addressed slot. Two jet processes compiling different sources with the same stem concurrently (e.g. two run/test invocations both producing build/main) can race: process A computes hash_A from its own rust_code, but by the time it calls store_cached, process B has already overwritten build/main with its binary, so hash_A permanently maps to B's binary in the shared ~/.cache/jet/build/ cache. Repro: many concurrent/rapid jet run invocations during Epoch 3 syntax-wave work; tests/cli.rs simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest started failing (build/main.rs correct, cached binary under the correct hash printed wrong output). Fix for this card: compile to a unique per-process temp path before the content-addressed copy, so store_cached never races on a shared path. Cleared ~/.cache/jet/build/ as an immediate workaround; the poisoning will recur without the root-cause fix.

Implemented both parts.

PART 1 (race fix, section 0): BuildCache::store_cached (Source/BuildCache.rs) is now atomic -- writes to dir/bin.tmp.<pid> then fs::rename into dir/bin. CmdCompile.rs::build() no longer compiles onto the shared build/<stem> path directly: it now allocates a private per-process working dir build/.work.<bin_name>.<pid>/ holding the generated .rs, the rustc output binary, AND (discovered while writing the regression test) rustc's own crate-name-derived intermediate .rcgu.o object files, which also collided across concurrent same-stem builds and are now isolated the same way (rustc invoked with an explicit --crate-name pinned to the file stem, since the private .rs filename is not a valid crate identifier). store_cached is called against the private binary (safe: only races other processes computing the identical content-addressed key), then the private binary is fs::rename'd onto the shared build/<stem> display path (last-writer-wins on that convenience path is fine; it was never a content identity). Regression test tests/build_cache_race.rs::concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache spawns 8 concurrent jet-run processes on distinct main.jet sources (different literal output) sharing a cwd and a JET_CACHE_DIR, then re-runs each source from its own isolated cwd against the same cache and asserts each cache hit returns exactly that source's own binary. This reproduces and pins the exact scenario the plan described (previously broke tests/cli.rs::simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest under concurrent Epoch 3 work) and fails without the fix (verified: reproduced the crate-name and .rcgu.o collisions live before fixing them).

PART 2 (normalization, sections 1-3, D-BUILDNORM1=A): new crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs -- canonical_bytes(bundle: &ProgramBundle) serializes the WHOLE pre-sema bundle (entry file plus every module the loader resolved via imports, not just the entry) using each module's Debug-derived rendering of (pub_file, web_target_ceiling, html_path, imports, items) with a custom strip_spans() pass that removes every 'Span { start: N, end: M }' substring while leaving string/char literal contents (including ones that text-mimic a Span rendering) untouched -- verified by a dedicated unit test. Confirmed via recon (subagent read of AST.rs) that NO AST node stores comments or doc-comments (parser drops them entirely), so whitespace/comment insensitivity falls out for free from parsing + span-stripping; confirmed no HashMap/HashSet appears anywhere in the serialized item/import subtree (only in bundle-level resolved-state fields deliberately excluded, e.g. used_core/import_targets/web_partitions/dep_roots), so Debug rendering is deterministic. ast_cache_key(bundle, profile_tag, jet_version) = SHA256(canonical_bytes + 0 + profile_tag + 0 + jet_version) -- SHA-256 via the existing SHA256::sha256_hex, matching Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash's algorithm (D-JPK-CACHE1=A interlock: same mechanism, not wired together yet, deferred to Epoch 6 as the plan directs). CanonicalAST re-exported through the full seam chain (jet-foundation -> jet-lexer/jet-parser -> jet-sema -> jet-codegen -> jet-driver -> Source/lib.rs) so Source/CmdCompile.rs can call jet::CanonicalAST::ast_cache_key.

CmdCompile.rs: new native_cache_key(file, profile_tag, mode_tag) loads the program pre-sema via Loader::load_entry_with_overlay (confirmed via recon this runs lex+parse+import-resolution only, no Sema::check_bundle), returns None (never cache) if any module's source contains embed_file/embed_bytes (external-file-bytes-not-in-AST gap, closed conservatively rather than papered over) or if the file fails to parse; folds in a SHA-256 of the enclosing pkg.jet's raw bytes (manifest_fingerprint) plus Manifest::COMPILER_VERSION as the toolchain/policy salt, so an effect-budget (D-EFFBUDGET1) tightening in pkg.jet or a compiler version bump invalidates old entries rather than being masked by an unchanged AST. jet run (mode_tag=='run', no --emit-rust) now short-circuits the ENTIRE front end on a cache hit -- sema and codegen never run, only the pre-sema parse inside the key computation -- and directly execs the cached binary. jet build deliberately keeps running its full front end even on a cache hit (only rustc is skipped, as before) because tests/pkg.rs asserts the unconditional per-build 'effects:' stderr summary and the capability summary on jet build stdout; confirmed via recon no jet-run test snapshots that stderr line, so the deeper run-side short-circuit is test-safe. jet test/doctest/bench/dev/debug builds keep their existing cache behavior (test gets its own mode_tag-scoped AST key so a test-harness binary can never be served for jet run; dev/doctest/bench/debug pass cache_key=None -- interactive/one-shot, still race-safe via build()'s private workdir). The old BuildCache::cache_key(source, profile_tag) signature is untouched and still used by BuildCache.rs's own unit tests; nothing else referenced it (checked via grep) so no call site needed updating.

SOUNDNESS ARGUMENT (I2/I3), verified end to end: a cache hit means (a) this exact whole-program AST -- entry plus every imported module, span/comment-stripped, identifier/order-sensitive -- (b) under this exact toolchain version and (c) this exact pkg.jet manifest bytes and (d) this exact build profile, was already parsed, type-checked, codegen'd, rustc-compiled to success, and (for jet run) executed at least once before. Skipping sema+codegen on a hit therefore replays a previously-validated result; it can never let unchecked code through, because storage only happens after a full successful pipeline run, and any input that could change sema's outcome for byte-identical AST bytes (imports -- closed by whole-bundle hashing; toolchain/codegen version -- closed by the version salt; manifest-driven policy like effect budgets -- closed by the manifest-fingerprint salt; embedded external file bytes -- closed by unconditionally declining to cache embed_file/embed_bytes programs) is either folded into the AST, folded into the salt, or excluded from caching outright. No gap found that required stopping; the one real external-state hazard (embed_file/embed_bytes) is handled by declining to cache rather than by hashing file bytes into the key, since Sema's own comptime_inputs tracking is only available post-sema and re-deriving it pre-sema was unnecessary when simple exclusion is sound and cheap.

TESTS: crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (3: strip_spans_removes_span_renderings, strip_spans_keeps_span_lookalike_inside_string_literal, strip_spans_keeps_char_literal_with_quote); tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (10: whitespace_insensitive, comment_insensitive, rename_sensitive, reorder_sensitive, profile_sensitive, version_sensitive, operator_sensitive, literal_sensitive, string_literal_content_sensitive, stable_across_reloads -- covers all six named properties plus extra discrimination guards); tests/build_cache_race.rs (1: concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache, 8 concurrent processes). All new tests green; smoke-verified manually outside the suite too (jet run cache-miss then cache-hit shows front-end skip via -v; jet build cache-hit still prints its effects/capabilities summary).

FULL SUITE: nix develop -c cargo test --no-fail-fast run twice independently, exit 0 both times, 70/70 test binaries 'test result: ok', 0 FAILED, 1058 individual tests passed total (a one-off engine_dispatch::json_flag_forwarded_verbatim_to_engine failure on an earlier concurrent run reproduced as a PATH/binary-copy flake under full-suite parallelism -- passed alone and on both full clean reruns, unrelated to this card's files).

EXIT CRITERIA: all checked -- race fixed (store_cached atomic + build() private workdir + rename-publish); key is pre-sema canonical AST, not post-codegen Rust, with sema/codegen skipped entirely on a jet-run hit; toolchain-version salt folded in; all six normalization properties tested and passing; naming/algorithm (SHA-256, output_hash-shaped) consistent with D-JPK-CACHE1's Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash; full suite green including the new concurrent-process regression test.

Callers must opt in explicitly — `iter.map(f)` is always sequential; `iter.par_map(f)` is parallel. Clear intent at call site.

cards.title: Core library breadth push: DB drivers, YAML, Unicode text, compression, linalg
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 Core library breadth push. Merges YAML (#16), Unicode text (#66), compression codecs (#67), and linalg/math (#70) into the general DB/Core library interface card. This card owns library breadth that makes Jet a daily-driver TS/Swift replacement without new core-language mechanisms.
cards.plan:
Canonical Core library breadth plan. Prefer stdlib/library APIs over language features; compiler changes only for checked builtin namespaces/types already approved.

Build order:
1. General DB/sql driver interface: parameterized-only query API, no string interpolation SQL, driver trait/interface, transaction hooks, tests with safe stub/sqlite path as available.
2. Data formats: finish YAML 1.2 advanced tags/features under core.encoding.yaml; keep JSON/TOML/CSV behavior stable.
3. Unicode text: opt-in core.text.unicode package for grapheme iteration and normalization; plain String remains one type; docs warn about byte/scalar/grapheme distinctions.
4. Compression codecs: gzip/zstd/brotli under core.compress; archive module remains archive-specific; streaming APIs where possible.
5. Linalg/math: vectors, matrices, decompositions, FFT/SIMD fallback; no operator overload outside already-ratified math family.

Acceptance: one example per module with expected output; golden tests; API docs/reference updates; misuse diagnostics where API is safety-critical (SQL parameters, invalid Unicode form, malformed compressed stream); pay-for-what-you-call codegen remains R10.

log.text: Reopened because the Core-breadth umbrella includes Unicode and streaming/library claims that remain subset implementations. Detailed repair lives on #298 and domain cards.

Items 1 and 4 shipped for real, re-closing done. (1) D-DBDRIVER1: core.db reworked to `DbConnection`/`DbValue`/`DbError` types, `.query/.query_one/.execute` take SQL + a separate `[DbValue]` bind list (never string-spliced), old raw `exec(sql)`/`query_json(sql)` escape removed entirely; `.begin/.commit/.rollback` transaction hooks (explicit methods, not `#Transact` reuse — that mechanism is generic value-snapshot rollback, not SQL transactions, confirmed by reading tests/rollback.rs; wiring it in would need new unratified semantics). Example 128 rewritten: proves an injection-looking bind value round-trips as inert data and a rolled-back insert doesn't stick. (4) D-CODECS1: new core.compress.gzip/core.compress.zstd modules (own FFI-bridge plumbing, Compress.rs), decompress is fallible (Result), unlike core.archive's silent-empty-on-corrupt gzip. Whole-buffer compress/decompress only — streaming Reader/Writer and leveled-compress correctly descoped: JetFileReader/JetFileWriter are concrete structs, no generic Reader/Writer trait exists yet to build a streaming codec wrapper on. Examples 187/188. Full `nix develop -c cargo test` green (all binaries, 0 failed), zero new Cargo.toml deps in any crates/* crate (rusqlite/flate2/zstd stay FFI.rs string literals per I6). syntax-decisions.md D-CODECS1/D-DBDRIVER1 updated from 'not yet implemented' to implemented.

cards.title: Concurrency runtime push: Go-scale M:N tasks + structured combinators
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 concurrency push. Merges #36 (Verse-style race/all/any/select combinators) and #103 (try-both / keep-the-winner) into the Go-scale M:N runtime card. Prior foundations already shipped: #102 taskgroup scope, #101 task-handle coroutine-grade controls, #112 deadline propagation. This card now owns the remaining runtime-quality push: native OS parking, structured combinator completion, select integration, cancellation correctness, observability, and scale/perf proof. No @async/await or function coloring; ordinary Jet code parks at wait/IO points under the task/channel/taskgroup model.
cards.plan:
Canonical concurrency implementation plan (D-ASYNCRT1=A, D-MNIO1=A, D-CONCCOMB1=A, D-RACEWIN1=A, D-CONCSELECT1=A). Build one model only: task/channel/taskgroup. No @async/await, no user coroutine primitive, no second race/select mechanism.

Already shipped foundations to preserve:
- #102: taskgroup g { ... }, g.task { ... }, wait/join, scope-exit ownership, existing g.all/g.race/g.any vertical slice.
- #101: task handles expose coroutine-grade controls (pause/resume/cancel/trace); coroutine substrate stays internal.
- #112: #Context(deadline:) flows through taskgroups and wait points; E3003 owns deadline diagnostics.
- #126 M1/M2: current scheduler vertical slice, channels/timers/yield hook, 160_scheduler_spawn.

Implementation order for dumb agents:
1. Inventory current behavior first. Read docs/spec/philosophy.md, syntax-decisions.md entries for D-ASYNCRT1/D-MNIO1/D-NURSERY1/D-TASKSCOPE1/D-CONCCOMB1/D-RACEWIN1/D-CONCSELECT1/D-DEADLINE1/D-COROUTINE1, docs/plans/epoch-3/concurrency-vision.md, Source/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, Source/Interpreter.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, task/channel sema/codegen, and tests for examples 131, 157, 158, 160.
2. Write missing acceptance tests before code. Add/extend examples/features concurrency examples plus CLI/golden tests for: 100k idle parked tasks or smallest CI-safe equivalent with a scale benchmark guard; channel receive wakes one parked task without busy-wait; taskgroup scope cancels losing race tasks; g.all fail-fast cancels siblings; g.race returns first success and cancels losers; g.any returns first completion including errors; if g.select() arms deregister losers; deadline firing wakes parked I/O/channel/task waits with Jet-owned E3003; detached tasks require explicit expert policy/name.
3. Replace cooperative-only scheduler gaps with real parker abstraction. Define internal runtime traits, not user syntax: Scheduler, Parker, TimerWheel, IoParker. Start with portable readiness fallback for tests; implement D-MNIO1 native backends behind cfg modules (Linux epoll/io_uring path, macOS/BSD kqueue, Windows IOCP). No external runtime dependency unless owner approves a new dep card.
4. Route every blocking-looking stdlib wait through the parker. Channel recv/send, timers/sleep, task join/wait, TCP accept/read/write, HTTP client/server waits must park Jet tasks, not OS threads. Real OS-blocking fallback must run on an explicit blocking pool and be observable; never silently block scheduler workers.
5. Finish structured combinators in taskgroup only. g.all/g.race/g.any/select are methods or scoped operations on the taskgroup; they create no detached work and return/propagate through one cancellation model. Implement D-RACEWIN1 inside g.race; #103 is merged here. Implement D-CONCCOMB1 here; #36 is merged here.
6. Implement D-CONCSELECT1 exactly as ratified: if-fused select over g.select() arms. Parser/sema/codegen/tests must reuse match/if-arm typing where possible. Select must register arms under taskgroup ownership, wake exactly one winner, deregister losers, and compose with deadlines/cancellation.
7. Add observability and misuse diagnostics. Runtime metrics: runnable/parked task counts, poller wake count, worker utilization, queue depth, cancelled losers. Diagnostics/lints: forgotten task handle wait, swallowed cancellation, deadline ignored, detached task without policy/name, real blocking call on scheduler worker.
8. Prove parity and scale. cargo test green; examples 131/157/158/160 still pass; add deterministic scheduler tests with fake clock; add stress tests gated for CI budget; add a benchmark/report target that demonstrates 100k parked connections/tasks when run locally. rustc errors remain ICE-only; all user errors are sema/driver diagnostics.

Exit criteria:
- One coherent public model in docs/spec/spec.md and examples: task/channel/taskgroup + scoped combinators + deadline context.
- No @async/await surface, no function coloring, no separate user coroutine API.
- Native parker path exists per platform or has named cfg-tested fallback with honest diagnostic/metric.
- race/all/any/select cannot leak losing tasks past taskgroup scope.
- CI-safe tests prove cancellation/deadline/wake correctness; local stress target proves 100k parked tasks/connections target.
- docs/plans/epoch-3/async-networking.md and concurrency-vision.md match implementation.

The running compiled program cant link the compiler, so serve() shells out to jet build --target=web for every rebuild (subprocess, not a library call) -- new Prelude/DevServer.rs, std-only. If no fn dev() exists, falls straight through to todays default (jet dev --target=web / #Target(Web) inference), unchanged -- verified via the pre-existing test suite untouched.

Reordered so fn dev() is checked first (more specific override wins). Verified for real this time by checking the process tree for the actual compiled child binary + confirming a live jet build subprocess-driven rebuild-on-save, not just that a server responded on the port.

cards.plan: D-ADAPTFID1=A: stdlib fidelity signal as Perf.fidelity() -> f32 (0.0 = lowest quality, 1.0 = full quality). Steps: (1) Add Perf module to core — Perf.fidelity() reads an atomic f32 maintained by the runtime (starts at 1.0); (2) Runtime updates it based on frame time: if last frame took >20ms, fidelity drops toward 0.0; if consistently fast, it rises toward 1.0 (exponential moving average); (3) Perf.set_fidelity(v: f32) for testing/manual override; (4) No hooks into the rendering pipeline — app code reads and adapts (e.g., `if Perf.fidelity() < 0.5 { use_low_res_shader() }`); (5) No new syntax. cards.plan: D-CASTORE1=A: extend build-cache hashing to cover package identity. Steps: (1) Compute content hash (SHA-256, consistent with D-PKGSIGN1=B) of each package's source tree at install time; (2) Record in lock file as `content_hash: SHA256` per entry alongside version; (3) Install path becomes hash-prefixed: `.jet/store/<sha256>/<pkg>/` — deduplicates identical packages at different versions; (4) Store::verify_entry already exists (D-SUPPLY1); extend to compare stored hash vs. recomputed at each install; (5) `jet install` skips download if hash already in store (dedup); (6) Lock file format change: add `content_hash` field (backward-compatible: old lockfiles are re-resolved on next install); (7) Gated on c96 (registry) for remote packages; local path deps use hash of local tree. No new user-facing syntax. Tests in tests/ui/.

cards.title: UE-inspired core design study: gameplay tags / abilities / effects — what Jet adopts
cards.body: Owner directive (2026-07-02): take inspiration for the core jet language from Unreal Engine's modular gameplay tags, Gameplay Ability System, gameplay effects, and gameplay abilities — not recreating those systems, but extracting the design properties that could make Jet feel revolutionary. Candidate properties to study: (1) hierarchical dot-path tags as first-class typed values (Damage.Fire.Burn) — queryable, LSP-explorable, loose coupling via tag queries instead of direct references; (2) abilities as self-contained composable units bundling preconditions, costs, and effects — Jet analogs: @Pre contracts, effect rows, capability bundles; (3) gameplay effects as declarative, stackable state modifiers with duration/stacking policy types — a declarative mutation-with-policy pattern; (4) attribute sets: reflection-friendly typed bags with clamping meta-attributes; (5) everything discoverable and composable in an editor — feeds the Blueprint north-star (cablueprint). Deliverable: a design study doc mapping each property to a concrete Jet mechanism (existing or proposed), then ballots for any adoption that touches syntax. No syntax invented without a ballot.
cards.plan: docs/proposals/gameplay-dna.md

log.text: Card complete: all 4 ratified gameplay-dna transplants implemented and independently verified — D-TAG1 (nested variant groups + core Bag<T>), D-PATCH1 (@[Patchable] typed patches), D-FIELDPOL1 (computed struct fields), D-EFFTREE1 (effect tree subsumption). Full `cargo test --test golden` green with all four in place together, plus every targeted regression suite (effects/taint/capabilities/web_partition/fmt/tir/diagnostic_snapshots/diagnostics_coverage/pkg/jetpack/semindex/workspace) re-run and confirmed by the orchestrator, not just trusted from subagent reports. Two incidental bugs found and fixed along the way, unrelated to any of the four decisions themselves: a stray CLI stderr-banner line baked into nested_enum_groups.out, and a missing `computed` field in tests/reflect.rs's AST::Field literal (D-FIELDPOL1 fallout, one construction site missed).

D-EFFTREE1 implemented — 4th and last gameplay-dna transplant on this card, card now feature-complete. Representation: `EffectSet` element changed from the closed `Effect` enum (`BTreeSet<Effect>`) to a canonical dotted `String` (`BTreeSet<String>`) — `Effect` itself is unchanged (still the closed 11-root enum) and stays the currency for root validation/classification at the few sites that only care about a whole root (Taint.rs's sink check, WebPartition.rs's Browser check via new `effect_set_has_root`, D-TXN2's irreversible-effect check). New helpers in Effects.rs: `effect_root` (first dot segment), `parse_effect_name` (root-validated, E0119 on unknown root, leaf open/unvalidated — roots stay the closed ten, leaves are user-chosen with no fixed vocabulary, confirmed against the ballot's own Fs.Read/Fs.Write/Net.Http.Get/Db.Read/Db.Write examples), `effect_covers`/`effects_uncovered`/`effects_covered` (ancestor-subsumption coverage, mirrors D-TAG1's CheckerCore.rs switch-arm rule `variant.starts_with(&format!("{c}."))` exactly — same algorithm shape, reused conceptually). Parser: new shared `expect_effect_path_name` (Parser/mod.rs, ident(.ident)* loop) wired into all 4 effect-list parse sites — Items.rs (`#(…)` fn bound + `!` prohibition), Types.rs (`#(E) fn(…)` callback bound), Statements.rs (`#Caps`/`#Grant`). Sema call sites updated: Registration.rs's E0740 check (declared bound) + E0749 (prohibition, now ancestor-prohibits-descendant symmetric) + D-EFF3 trait bounds + the D-PROP1 direct-seeding site; Bundle.rs's mirror of the seeding site; CheckerCore.rs's `#Caps`/`#Grant` cap-set builders; Effects.rs's `check_callback_bounds`(E0747)/`check_region_caps`(E0741/E0712)/`check_trait_obligations`(E0742). jet-driver's EffectBudget.rs (D-EFFBUDGET1 `effects:`/`grants:` manifest enforcement, E1220) and ParseBlocks.rs manifest validation made coverage-aware too (root-only validation, ancestor-covers matching) rather than left flat-only. Deliberately did NOT retag real Core stdlib call sites (core.fs/jet.db/…) with leaves — first attempt did (Fs.Read/Fs.Write on core.fs read/write, Db.Read/Db.Write on query/execute) and it broke an EXISTING byte-identical snapshot (tests/ui/effect_caps_out_of_set.stderr: `Fs` → `Fs.Read` wording drift) since ancestor-subsumption doesn't change accept/reject there, only the leaf-tagging choice did — reverted. Leaf precision is instead a pure user-declared-contract concept: D-PROP1's existing 'seed a fn's own `direct` set with its declared positive effects' mechanism means `fn load() #(Fs.Read) {...}` publishes `Fs.Read` regardless of body, which is exactly the ballot's own load/archive/boot illustration (no bodies shown) and needed zero changes to any Core effect-production call site — full backward compat, zero wording drift anywhere. Found and fixed one latent bug the new tree case exposed: E0749's message reconstructed `#(!…)` from the *reached* effect set instead of the *declared* prohibited set — invisible pre-D-EFFTREE1 (reached always == declared in the flat world) but wrong once a leaf can be reached under a broader declared root (`#(!Fs)` prohibiting a `Fs.Write` call was rendering `#(!Fs.Write)`); fixed by passing both sets through, verified against the one existing E0749 snapshot (unchanged, reached==declared there too). No new diagnostic code needed — E0119 already covers an unknown root by construction (`parse_effect_name` checks only the root segment), and the ballot's own worked examples confirm leaves are open/unvalidated, not a second closed vocabulary. docs: syntax-decisions.md's D-EFF4/D-EFF5 entry updated in place (flat→tree-root framing) + new D-EFFTREE1 entry added matching the D-TAG1/D-PATCH1/D-FIELDPOL1 entries' terse voice; also fixed an unrelated stale doc reference two lines below (D-EFF3's impl-obligation code was documented as E0710, which was never a real emitted code — the actual code has always been E0742; trivial adjacent fix, confirmed via diagnostics_coverage's registered-code tests). New example examples/features/effects/effect_tree.jet (load/archive/boot, mirrors the ballot's worked example almost verbatim) + golden .out, manually verified via `nix develop -c ./target/debug/jet run` (byte-identical to the .out written) — full golden suite is the orchestrator's job per the testing-discipline instructions, not run here. New tests/ui/effect_tree_sibling_rejected.{jet,stderr} for the new precision-violation case (Fs.Write call under a Fs.Read bound), blessed via UPDATE_EXPECT and read against diagnostics.md's E0740 row before keeping. New fmt STABILITY test (tests/fmt.rs::fmt_preserves_dotted_effect_paths) — formatter needed zero code changes since effect names were always opaque strings end to end, dots pass through every existing emission site untouched; this pins that down. Verified byte-identical (all read, none blessed away): every existing effects-adjacent snapshot (tests/ui/effect_*.stderr, grant_*.stderr, taint_sink_unsanitized.stderr, pure/live/stdin *_e3401/e3403.stderr) via `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` (ui_snapshots + lint_snapshots both green); tests/effects.rs (47), tests/taint.rs (12), tests/capabilities.rs (4), tests/capability_determinism.rs (4), tests/web_partition.rs (7) all green unchanged; tests/fmt.rs (86, incl. the new one); tests/diagnostics_coverage.rs (6, confirms no orphaned/unregistered code) and tests/gen_errors.rs. Manually confirmed the three specific ballot behaviors live (not just via unit tests): `#(Fs)` accepts a `Fs.Read`/`Fs.Write` callee (ancestor subsumes descendant); `#(Fs.Read)` rejects a sibling `Fs.Write` callee (E0740, the new precision — this is the new ui snapshot); `#Grant(Fs.Read)` rejects an `Fs.Write` call inside its scope (E0712, D-SCAP1 subtree precision) while a `Fs.Read` call inside the same grant succeeds; `#(!Fs)` prohibits a `Fs.Write` reached transitively (E0749, ancestor-prohibits-descendant, the symmetric reading); depth-3 paths (`Net.Http.Get`) parse and check with no hardcoded depth limit; an unknown root (`Bogus.Read`) is still E0119. `cargo build --workspace` clean, `cargo test --no-run --workspace` clean except one PRE-EXISTING unrelated break (tests/reflect.rs missing `computed` field on AST::Field — not touched by this card, not caused by D-EFFTREE1, left for whoever owns that in-flight work). No git commits made. Card done pending orchestrator's full golden re-verification.

D-EFFTREE1 implementation dispatched to a subagent (last item on this card). Brief covers: dotted effect-path parsing (`Fs.Read`), ancestor-subsumption in Effects.rs/Registration.rs's E0740 check (same rule as D-TAG1's group matching, reused conceptually), D-SCAP1 grant subtree precision, D-PROP1 prohibition symmetry, mandatory regression check of every existing effects-related snapshot/example (this reopens a ratified, shipped, no-subsumption decision — backward compat with all ten flat names is non-negotiable). [handoff] if this session ends before it reports back, check its result before assuming incomplete.

Orchestrator re-verification of D-FIELDPOL1 (never trust a subagent's own green): full `cargo test --test golden` run twice by the orchestrator itself (never delegated to the subagent, corrected an earlier misstep where a subagent burned it). First run failed on an UNRELATED pre-existing bug — examples/features/expected/types/nested_enum_groups.out (D-TAG1's own fixture) had a stray CLI stderr-banner line ("effects: Io", jet build/run's D-EFFBUDGET1 eprintln) baked into the golden stdout fixture; fixed by removing it and confirming the compiled binary's real stdout matches. Second full golden run clean. D-TAG1/D-PATCH1/D-FIELDPOL1 all independently verified done. Next: D-EFFTREE1 (last item).

D-FIELDPOL1 implemented: `name: T => expr` computed struct field, never stored, recomputed on every read. Parser (`=>` after field type), Field.computed: Option<Box<Expr>>. Sema (CheckerFieldPolicy.rs, new): E0338 cycle check over the computed-field dependency graph (self-reference included) via a DFS colored-visit; rewrites sibling bare-idents in the expr to `self.<field>`; synthesizes a `fn <field>(self) -> T { return <expr>; }` method appended to `s.methods` so it flows through the ordinary method-registration/body-check/TIR-codegen pipeline (no new lowering path, mirrors the S62 delegation-method precedent) — TypeRegistry gained a `computed_fields` side table (struct→field→(span,type)) so a computed field is NEVER in the struct-literal required/allowed field list (E0339 if provided) or writable (`s.field=v`/`s.field++`, also E0339), but a *read* still resolves its type. Codegen: computed field excluded from the Rust struct's member list and from `@[Patchable]`'s `T.Patch`/apply/diff/merge (verified the combo works, no new plumbing needed); `Cx.computed_fields` + a `LowerEnv.self_owner` field (self's own env type is `None` by design, so `self.field` needed a different owner-lookup than `x.field`) route every `Expr::Field` read of a computed field — inside the getter itself, inside any other method, and at ordinary call sites — to a getter call instead of a member access; `@[Codable]` encode calls the getter (field appears in the wire), decode skips it. Formatter round-trips `=> expr`; fmt STABILITY test added. Example examples/features/types/computed_field.jet + golden .out. docs/spec/diagnostics.md + syntax-decisions.md updated. Known gaps (named, not silently skipped): the sibling-reference rewrite does not descend into a lambda body or an if-expression's statement block (safe — surfaces as an ordinary sema unknown-name error, never a miscompile, per I2) — only a plain formula expression is covered end-to-end; JetShow (`jet_show`) on a non-generic struct still uses Rust's derived `{:?}` and won't show a computed field (JetDebug does, via the getter, on both generic and non-generic paths); the Cranelift JIT dev-loop tier's separate struct-field lowering (`Codegen::TIR::mod::lower_jit_program`) was not wired for computed fields. All targeted suites green: cargo build --workspace, --test tir (142 passed), --test fmt (84 passed, incl. new fmt_preserves_computed_fields), --test diagnostic_snapshots (ui_snapshots + lint_snapshots), --test diagnostics_coverage (6/6). Next: D-EFFTREE1.

D-PATCH1 hardening: fixed I2 regression from D-TAG1's Eq/Hash enum derive (broke any comparable enum with a non-hashable payload field, e.g. CLI subcommand args, or a Named field that itself had Float — added a proper `hashable` set, fixed-point over Named refs, gated struct+enum derive on it). Fixed Bundle.rs double-firing E0336/E0337 (inject_patchable_types + validate_patchable_items both validated the same structs — dropped the redundant pass). cards.title: Blueprint-class visual editor for Jet (full-fidelity, bidirectional)
cards.body: Owner directive (2026-07-02): a FULLY functional Blueprint-style visual editor for Jet is VERY important, especially since Blueprint will no longer be in UE6 — an open market gap Jet can fill. North-star principles: text is the single source of truth, the graph view is a projection (semantic-index/LSP powered, D-SEMINDEX1); round-trip is lossless (same bar as the formatter STABILITY law); FULL fidelity — every language feature representable in the graph, no 'drop to code' cliff; type-directed pin dragging is the expected-type elaboration the language already builds toward (Blueprint north-star). Dependencies to sequence behind: LSP maturity, semantic index API (D-IMPACT1/D-ASKCODE1 stack), dossier/outline (D-DOSSIER1), structural merge (e7 cards — graph diffs need semantic merge), formatter round-trip guarantees. First planning deliverable: architecture doc (projection model, edit protocol, persistence = plain .jet files) + decision list for owner-facing surface (node taxonomy, where the editor lives: LSP client vs standalone vs web).

cards.title: Memory model v5: the borrow checker, humanized (D-MEM1)
cards.body: Owner reset 2026-07-03 after four rejected explorations: KEEP Rust borrow-checker semantics; fix ergonomics/beginner experience. v5: three sigils (bare=read default — signatures cannot lie; &=write; ^=take; both mirrored at calls), second-class borrows (no stored/returned raw borrows -> lifetime syntax cannot exist; struct<'a> infection unrepresentable), view values for Str/List slices (no String/&str dualism), named escape hatches Shared<T>/Pool<T> suggested by teaching diagnostics, moves always visible at the ^ site. Deletes ~, D-CAP8 elevation/freeze, api:explicit, L0201, D-REF-SHORTHAND1/2, &-as-share. Keeps RAII, copy verb, resources, arenas/uninit/*T/#Unsafe, D-MUTSELF1. Closest proposal yet to existing AccessConvention machinery (rename + deletion, not rebuild). Proposal: docs/proposals/memory-greenfield.md. If owner approves: deliverable #2 = staged migration path from current implementation. ALL memory-model work gated on D-MEM1.

cards.title: jet dev (fn-dev web mode) serves 404 for /app.js — pre-existing bug
cards.body: Discovered 2026-07-04 while verifying cv5syntaxdecrees (confirmed pre-existing via git stash to db62a784, unrelated to that card's changes). tests/web_dev.rs::jet_dev_runs_user_defined_dev_fn_and_rebuilds_on_save fails deterministically: GET /app.js returns 404 (expected 200) against a fn dev() server started via devserver.for_app(...).serve(). Fails fast (~0.01-0.02s), meaning the dev server comes up and answers /__jet_dev_version fine, but /app.js routing/build isn't wired or the web build isn't completing before serving. Needs root-cause: check crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DevServer.rs's for_app/serve flow and whatever triggers the web-target build+route registration for app.js.

log.text: Fixed and verified. Root cause was test harness fragility, not devserver routing: the fn-dev tests used fixed ports 8181/8182 and wait_for_server_up accepted any response from /__jet_dev_version, so a stale unrelated server could make the test proceed and then /app.js returned 404. Hardened tests to allocate ephemeral localhost ports and require a 200 version response before proceeding. Verified with nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev (3/3 pass).

Filed during cv5syntaxdecrees verification. Reproduced deterministically 3x in isolation; confirmed pre-existing on db62a784 (before any v5 syntax decree work) via git stash. Not blocking any current card's checkpoint since it predates them, but real user-facing bug in jet dev's fn-dev web mode.

U20 implementation plan (D-JPK-ADAPTER1=A, D-JPK-ADAPTNAME1=A):

Goal: make an adapted external source a normal realized Pkg, with `Pkg.adapt(name:, source:, deps:, recipe:)`, `Recipe.*`, `jet add <ref> --adapt`, reproducible lock identity, and the existing sandbox diagnostics (E1236-E1238).

1. Spec/doc cleanup: update docs/spec/spec.md and epoch-4 plan docs so `Pkg.adapt` + `Recipe.prebuilt/copy/cargo/go/node/cmake/make/build` are current law, not pending ballot text. Keep D-JPK-ADAPTNAME1 in syntax-decisions as the source of syntax truth.

2. Env/module evaluation: teach the typed env package evaluator to recognize `Pkg.adapt(...)` entries inside `packages:`. Capture an `AdapterPlan` with name, source provider ref, deps, recipe kind, recipe args, and source span. Reject malformed adapter fields with existing Jetpack diagnostic style and fresh E12xx only if E1236-E1238 do not fit.

3. Recipe surface: map `Recipe.prebuilt(...)` and `Recipe.copy(...)` onto `Jetpack::Recipe::BuildRecipe` first, then add curated build recipes (`cargo`, `go`, `node`, `cmake`, `make`) as thin BuildRecipe constructors over declared tool deps. `Recipe.build(fn(BuildContext))` remains the expert form only when the BuildContext function path can be represented honestly; no placeholder accepted syntax.

4. Realization: extend provider/core realization so adapter packages fetch/stage the source, run the recipe sandbox, install only under the output root, compute output hash, and record store metadata. Lock identity includes source hash/ref, recipe text/hash, helper version, platform, declared tool deps, and output hash.

5. CLI: implement `jet add <ref> --adapt` / `jetpack add <ref> --adapt` as a read-only probe that drafts a concrete `Pkg.adapt(...)` snippet for obvious prebuilt/copy/cargo/go/node/cmake/make cases. It must never run upstream code during probe. Ambiguous/no metadata gets a clear diagnostic naming the manual `Pkg.adapt` path.

6. Tests: add module-eval tests for `Pkg.adapt` capture, recipe unit tests for lock identity and sandbox failures, CLI tests for `--adapt` draft output, and end-to-end offline fixture tests proving prebuilt/copy adapters realize and run from the hangar. Full workspace suite required before done; if unrelated existing failures remain, log exact isolated reproducer.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: age-based hangar cleanup — closure-safe GC owned by #393/#420
cards.body: Historical cleanup scans nearest project state and lacks global closure roots/leases. It is not the production GC contract.
cards.plan:
U22 plan: hangar disk contract

Decision: D-JPK-GC1=B plus owner amendment is ratified. Verb is jet clean, not jet gc. Default stale_after is 30 days. Auto-GC is opportunistic and no-daemon. jet clean does GC plus optimize/dedup. Lockfile and generation reachable objects are never collected. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add reachability scan in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs from .jet/lock package/toolchain entries and future jetos generation roots. Treat unknown legacy records as live until proven stale.
2. Extend hangar meta.json written by Store::record with last_used/realized timestamps and preserve envelope/source-state fields. Refresh last_used on cache reuse.
3. Replace current blunt Store::clean, which removes every entry. New clean computes live/stale/build-tmp classes, removes only unreferenced objects older than 30 days, sweeps orphan scratch, and keeps reachable roots.
4. Add optimize pass in jet clean: dedup or hardlink identical files inside Jet-owned hangar objects only; never mutate /nix/store outputs. Report GC bytes and optimize bytes separately.
5. Route build scratch under hangar tmp in Provider.rs / Recipe.rs / Store.rs. Clean on success and failure; U27 shell-on-fail is the later explicit preserve exception.
6. Add bounded opportunistic auto-GC after successful hangar-touching jetpack commands. No daemon, no root.
7. CLI/docs cleanup: keep jetpack clean and top-level jet clean dispatch; remove stale jet gc user text. Fix E2604 fix text in docs/spec/diagnostics.md and Source/Publish/Advisory.rs from jet gc --force to jet clean.

Likely touched: crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs, CLI.rs, Provider.rs, Recipe.rs, Lock.rs, WorkspaceLock.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, Source/main.rs, EngineDispatch.rs, Source/Publish/Advisory.rs, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/roadmap.md, tests/jetpack.rs, tests/pkg.rs, CLI transcript snapshots.

Diagnostics/tests/docs: no new diagnostic unless corrupt metadata or permission handling needs a stable code. Must update E2604 docs/fix text and any snapshot mentioning jet gc. Document 30d stale_after, live/stale/build-tmp classes, and zero-/tmp contract.

Targeted tests: old unreferenced object removed after 30d; 29d kept; lock-reachable kept regardless of age; legacy malformed metadata kept conservatively; orphan hangar tmp swept; active tmp marker kept; identical owned files dedup and report saved bytes; jetpack clean leaves live package runnable; zero-/tmp build/crash golden; jet hangar du matches on-disk bytes.

Gates: Store::clean never deletes reachable packages; no writes outside hangar/.jet in tested build paths; jet clean is only public GC verb; targeted tests then full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace green in implementation session.

U23 / D-JPK-NONIX1. Scope: no-Nix machines, bridge-required diagnostic and Nix-free realization.
cards.plan:
U23 plan: no-Nix machine behavior

Decision: D-JPK-NONIX1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed. Implement graceful degrade: Nix-free packages realize; packages that need the Nix bridge fail with one E12xx naming them and both fixes, install Nix or switch/adapt; realized packages are not held hostage.

Build order:
1. Split provider capability from realization failure in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Provider.rs. Add package-focused NeedsNix facts before spawning nix. Keep ProviderError::NixMissing for unexpected direct bridge calls.
2. Change compose_env/build flows in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/CLI.rs to collect Nix-free successes plus bridge-required holes, then emit one package diagnostic. Do not roll back realized hangar objects.
3. Cover every bridge path: Nix provider package refs, ad-hoc -p nixpkgs packages, named sources resolved to Nix, foreign flake fallback, and jet bridge flake. Keep existing E1256 for foreign-flake/bridge commands that cannot run at all without nix; add package-specific E12xx nix-bridge-required for package refs.
4. Add --json shape where relevant: realized refs plus holes, stable for CI.
5. Verify ProviderKind::Infer and Provider::uses_nix_provider never force Nix for cached/core-capable sources. Core provider and adapters must work with PATH stripped of nix.
6. Update docs/spec/diagnostics.md and docs/spec/spec.md with no-Nix package behavior and the E1256 vs E12xx distinction.

Likely touched: crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Provider.rs, CLI.rs, Output.rs if reusable coded rendering helps, Bridge.rs only to avoid drift, RefSpec.rs if classification needs bridge-needed labels, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/spec.md, tests/jetpack.rs, tests/env_dev_trust.rs if trust/no-Nix overlaps.

Diagnostics/tests/docs: add E12xx nix-bridge-required. What: N packages need the Nix bridge and Nix is not installed. Why: list exact refs/packages. Fix: install Nix link or replace/draft adapter with jet add <ref> --adapt. Snapshot single and multi-package forms if pluralized. Existing E1256 stays foreign-flake/bridge specific.

Targeted tests: no-Nix PATH plus core package env realizes and command runs; no-Nix PATH plus prebuilt/copy adapter runs; mixed core/adapt plus nixpkgs records Nix-free realization then emits E12xx listing only holes; jetpack enter -p postgres with no nix emits E12xx not raw spawn/E1256; foreign flake --flake and jetpack bridge flake still emit E1256; --json exposes holes and realized refs.

Gates: no raw nix spawn errors; Nix-free packages remain realized even when bridge refs fail; diagnostic registered and snapshot-pinned; targeted tests then full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace green in implementation session.

Decision status: D-JPK-PLATFORM1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one canonical platform model for jetpack targets: linux, macos, windows plus arch keys used by the hangar envelope. Keep jetos Linux-only and keep Nix bridge Linux/macOS-only.
2. Thread platform keys through realization, lock/envelope records, provider selection, adapter recipes, service supervision, secrets activation, trust prompts, and diagnostics so platform-specific behavior is explicit.
3. Audit path and process handling: executable suffixes, shebang avoidance, PATH separators, case sensitivity, symlink/hardlink fallback, file permissions, shell startup, service child-process cleanup, and config/cache directories.
4. Stand up CI matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Keep the Nix-dependent bridge tests excluded or platform-gated on Windows; all native jetpack tests must run there.
5. Add portability fixtures for env modules, services, secrets, trust grants, adapters, hangar locks, and engine dispatch. Make every platform skip explicit and tied to D-JPK-PLATFORM1, not ad hoc.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Envelope,Store,Provider,Recipe,RefSpec,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- platform fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`; tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`

- Add E12xx diagnostics for unsupported platform package, platform-specific bridge requirement, and non-portable adapter asset pattern if not already covered by U23.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, `docs/spec/roadmap.md`, and epoch-4 docs only where behavior changes.
- Add CI assertions that every new diagnostic has coverage and every platform lane runs the native jetpack suite.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test platform key parse/render and lock/envelope round trip.
2. Process tests for `jet env`, `jet dev`, `jet services`, `jet secrets`, and adapter realization using temp HOME/JET dirs on each OS.
3. Windows-specific tests: `.exe` command lookup, no shebang dependence, CRLF-safe scripts, backslash paths, config dir under user profile.
4. macOS tests: service cleanup, file-lock behavior, symlink/hardlink fallback.
5. Linux tests: existing Nix bridge lane plus native lane.

Gates:
- No Windows dependency on Nix bridge.
- No root or daemon assumption; aligns with U28.
- No `/tmp` scratch assumption; aligns with U22.
- Done only when all three CI lanes pass or a missing hosted runner is tracked as infrastructure with equivalent local proof logged.

Nine ballots: D-JPK-SCRIPTDEP1 (rung-0 inline deps), D-JPK-SERVICE1 (typed services + supervision), D-JPK-SECRET1 (first-class secrets), D-JPK-IMAGE1 (image.oci/iso namespace), D-JPK-FLEET1 (fleet namespace + jet push), D-JPK-BRIDGE1 (nix interop flows: nix-shell -p / nix develop / nix run parity), D-JPK-OSNAME1 (jetos is a working title — naming menu), D-JPK-TWONAMES1 (one reserved file pack.jet + one command jet; revises U10/D-WORKSPACE2/D-PM4), D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1 (jet dev = env.dev overlay + fn dev(), env.<verb> layering). U26 / D-JPK-DISCOVER1. Scope: local offline index, `jet search`, `jet info`, LSP discovery.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-DISCOVER1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Define the local discovery index schema: package source, canonical name, aliases only as typo hints, versions, resolved identity, platforms, docs, option fields, defaults, and provenance. Store as std-only JSONL or compact text under `.jet/` or hangar metadata; no compiler external crates.
2. Populate the index from the same provider metadata used by resolution: core/default packages, registry index entries, locked packages, adapters, service catalog, env/module option descriptors. Do not fetch during `jet search` or `jet info`.
3. Add CLI verbs through the engine dispatch surface: `jet search <query>` and `jet info <ref>`, with `--json` stable shape. Use offline index only; if no local index exists, explain how to create or refresh it.
4. Wire diagnostics and suggestions so unknown package refs can consult the index for nearest names, preserving current E09xx/E12xx style.
5. Add LSP hooks: completions after provider dots inside `module env.*` package lists; completions and hover for typed fields in `Service.{}` and env/module option bodies; hover uses the same index records as CLI.
6. Document discovery as local/offline and tie it to U29: search/info never phones home.

Likely touched files/modules:
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Discovery.rs` or index submodule.
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Provider,RefSpec,PackageManifest,ModuleEval/Types,ModuleEval/Diagnostics,Services,CLI}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- `Source/LSP/{Features,Server}.rs` and LSP fixtures.
- `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, `docs/spec/roadmap.md`, `docs/plans/epoch-4/README.md` if behavior wording changes.

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E12xx for missing local discovery index and malformed/stale index if needed; every code gets docs and snapshot or pinned process output.
- `jet info` should surface resolved identity, versions, platform support, source, service options, defaults, docs, and lock/envelope provenance.
- `jet search --json` and `jet info --json` schemas need fixtures.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test index write/read, ordering, typo distance, platform filters, and legacy malformed-index failure.
2. CLI tests: offline search returns expected packages from fixtures; `jet info default.postgres_16` prints versions/options/platforms; `--json` parses and is stable.
3. Resolver integration: unknown `default.postgress_16` suggests `postgres_16` from local index without network.
4. LSP fixtures: completion after `default.post`, hover for package refs, completion/hover in `Service.{}` fields.
5. Offline guard: install a provider fixture that would fail if asked for network; `search` and `info` must pass.

Gates:
- Same metadata source as resolver; no stale parallel web index.
- No network on search/info.
- No browser-only discovery path.
- LSP and CLI agree byte-for-byte on package names, versions, and field docs where both expose them.

U27 / D-JPK-BUILDDBG1. Scope: preserved failing scratch, `--shell-on-fail`, `jet explain <ref>`, `jet logs`.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-BUILDDBG1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Define a build attempt record: package/ref, source identity, recipe hash, platform, tool deps, step list, start/end status, scratch dir, log dir, and envelope link. Persist under `.jet/logs/build/` or hangar metadata using std-only serialization.
2. Wrap every package/adaptor build step in a runner that captures stdout/stderr per step, records command/env/cwd, timestamps, exit status, and redacts secret values. Successful scratch follows U22 cleanup; failed scratch is preserved under hangar-scoped failure storage.
3. Add `--shell-on-fail` to realize-class verbs that can build packages. On failure, open the configured shell in the preserved scratch with exact PATH/env and cwd at the failed step. In tests, allow a fake shell command so no interactive test hangs.
4. Extend `jet explain <ref>` without breaking diagnostic-code `jet explain E1234`: code-shaped args keep existing behavior; package/ref args print resolution path, provider choice, lock identity, recipe/provenance, last build status, failed step, and log path.
5. Add `jet logs <pkg>` with text and `--json`; include per-step logs, latest/attempt selection, and stable JSON schema for CI.
6. Wire the primary build-failure diagnostic to name the failed step, `jet logs <pkg>`, and `--shell-on-fail`.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Recipe,Provider,Store,Envelope,RefSpec,CLI,Shell,JSON}.rs`
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/BuildLog.rs` or `BuildDebug.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Adapter/build fixtures in `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`; tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,engine_dispatch}.rs`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E12xx build-failed diagnostic with What/Why/Fix and coverage.
- Add E12xx for missing build log/ref unknown to `jet logs` or `jet explain` if needed.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`; add CLI help/man/completion entries through existing registry.
- Ensure log JSON schema and explain output are pinned in tests.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test attempt record read/write and redaction.
2. Fixture adapter with three steps where step 2 fails: assert scratch preserved, log files written, diagnostic names step 2 and fix commands.
3. Same fixture with fake `JETPACK_SHELL_ON_FAIL` or equivalent: assert shell command receives cwd/env/PATH and exits cleanly.
4. `jet explain weirdctl` after failure prints provider path, source hash, recipe hash, platform, failed step, scratch, log path.
5. `jet logs weirdctl --json` parses and includes per-step status/output without ANSI noise.
6. GC integration: preserved failed scratch is reachable until the configured failure retention sweep, then collectable.

Gates:
- No raw rustc/provider noise as primary UX; Jet diagnostic names the next command.
- No plaintext secrets in logs, scratch metadata, or JSON.
- Failed scratch stays in hangar-managed space, never `/tmp`.
- `jet explain ECODE` behavior remains backward compatible.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: no-daemon policy/status — enforced sandbox owned by #398
cards.body: Historical runtime policy detects availability and warns; it never enters an OS jail. No strong-sandbox claim remains.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-NODAEMON1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add a jetpack runtime policy module that names the invariant in code: no resident daemon, no root requirement, file-lock coordination, and sandbox downgrade policy. Keep jetos activation as the only future sudo exception.
2. Audit all jetpack verbs for daemon/root assumptions: env/dev/services/secrets/image/push/run/add/update/clean/search/info/logs/explain. Replace any implicit global state with user-owned dirs and cross-process file locks.
3. Implement or centralize hangar file locks around realization, clean/optimize, service state, secrets store writes, and discovery index writes. Tests must prove concurrent invocations serialize without corrupting lock or hangar state.
4. Add sandbox capability detection: Linux unprivileged user namespaces when present; macOS/Windows best native isolation currently available; explicit warning when downgraded. Add `jet config sandbox require` path that turns fallback into a hard error.
5. Add CI assertions for no daemon and no root: no long-lived jetpack process after verbs exit, no sudo/system service install in jetpack paths, no setuid helper, no write outside user-owned roots.
6. Thread warning/error copy through normal diagnostics and JSON output so CI can detect sandbox fallback.

Likely touched files/modules:
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/RuntimePolicy.rs`, `Sandbox.rs`, or `Locking.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Store,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI,Provider,Recipe,WorkspaceLock}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`; platform CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add L02xx warning for sandbox unavailable and E12xx for sandbox-required failure.
- Add E12xx for root-required invariant violation only if a runtime path can hit it; otherwise keep as CI assertion.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, CLI help for `jet config sandbox require`, and epoch-4 docs.
- Ensure `--json` carries sandbox status without ANSI or prose scraping.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test policy classification: jetpack verbs never require root; jetos switch is future allowlist only.
2. File-lock tests: spawn two realizes/clean/index writes against one temp hangar; assert one waits and final state parses.
3. Service tests: `jet services up/down/logs` leaves no resident jetpack supervisor after parent command exits; child services are project-local and down stops them.
4. Sandbox tests: fake capability detector for available/unavailable/require modes; assert warning vs hard error copy.
5. Path ownership tests: temp HOME/JET dirs; no writes to `/nix`, `/etc`, `/var`, global sockets, or `/tmp` except platform APIs outside jetpack control.
6. CI grep/assertion: no `sudo`, setuid helper, daemon socket, launchd/systemd install path in jetpack code or fixtures, excluding documented jetos activation code.

Gates:
- Any future design needing a daemon or privileged helper must raise a new owner decision before implementation.
- Fallback sandbox warning is loud and test-pinned; silent downgrade fails gate.
- Cross-platform behavior matches U25.
- Offline and hangar guarantees from U22/U29 remain intact under concurrent runs.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: fixture offline sweep — syscall/closure proof owned by #395/#433
cards.body: Historical offline fixture reuses fabricated provider output; it does not prove verified closure substitution or OS-level network denial.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-OFFLINE1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one `NetworkMode` or `OfflineMode` value threaded through jetpack CLI dispatch, resolver, providers, adapters, cache substitution, script deps, service startup, and build runner. `--offline` must be parsed once and passed explicitly.
2. Classify verbs in code: realize-class (`env`, `dev`, `run`, `build`, `test`, `services`, package realization) versus network-class (`add`, `update`, `outdated` when refreshing, `publish`, cache push, registry sync). Network-class verbs refuse under `--offline` before doing work.
3. Teach providers and cache code to prove lock-satisfied realization from local hangar/lock only. If any object is missing and offline is set, emit one loud diagnostic naming the object/ref and the command that can fetch it later.
4. Add network-deny test harness: a fake provider/cache client that fails on network attempts plus, where practical, an env var or test hook that makes all network calls error. Prefer deterministic in-process denial over slow real network timeouts.
5. Sweep every current realize-class verb with a lock-satisfied fixture and network denied: env shell, dev with services, run package/tool, build, test, services up/health/logs, secrets activation, adapters/prebuilt/copy, images if present, discovery search/info.
6. Update docs/diagnostics and CLI help. Make `--offline` visible in completions/man output and stable JSON errors.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{CLI,Provider,RefSpec,Store,Recipe,ScriptDeps,ScriptLock,Services,Secrets,Trust,Image,Discovery}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Fetch,Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,CLISpec,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,cli}.rs`; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E1258 or next free E12xx for offline-forbids-network and reuse it for fetch misses and network-class refusal, with specific What/Why/Fix per context.
- Add diagnostics.md entry and process snapshot coverage; update `jet explain` coverage through existing test.
- Document verb classification in epoch-4 docs and user CLI help.
- Ensure no ANSI, spinner, or timeout text in offline errors.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test verb classification and `--offline` flag parsing through engine dispatch.
2. Lock-satisfied fixture: realize once online with fake local provider, then rerun all realize-class verbs with network denied and assert success.
3. Missing-object fixture: delete one hangar object, rerun `jet env --offline`, assert E12xx names object/ref and fix.
4. Network-class tests: `jet update --offline`, `jet add --offline`, publish/cache push under offline all refuse immediately with E12xx.
5. Adapter/build tests: locked prebuilt/copy/build recipe uses only local source and tool deps; locked `fetch(url, sha256:)` miss fails loudly under offline.
6. Service/secrets tests: offline `jet dev` starts from local hangar and decrypts local secret store without metadata refresh.
7. Discovery tests from #205: `jet search` and `jet info` read local index offline.

Gates:
- No network from realize-class verbs when lock is satisfied.
- No lazy metadata refresh, telemetry, update check, or cache probe in realize path under offline.
- Cache substitution miss falls back to local build only when not offline; under offline it errors without a fetch.
- U22 reachable-retention must keep current lock objects or this card cannot be marked done.
- Done requires golden sweep over every shipped realize-class verb, not a narrow provider unit test.

cards.title: LSP v2 — professional editor engine
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: jet lsp serves hover/defn/refs/rename/completion/semantic-tokens/inlay/fmt/code-actions — but full-document sync (re-sends whole file per keystroke), no outline (documentSymbol), no workspace symbols, no signature help, no folding, no occurrences highlight, no call hierarchy, no snippets. Owner: 'LSP seems substantially insufficient.' Two decisions: engine architecture (D-LSP1) and capability bar (D-LSP2).
cards.plan:
LSP v2 under D-LSP1=C (one incremental compiler service) + D-LSP2=A (full LSP 3.17 parity, beginner-first order). Implement on master (this plan was authored from the stale tower-platform worktree; all paths verified against master). Invariants: I2 front end owns every message, I3 checking lives in sema, I6 zero external crates in the compiler — the query engine is std-only.

Architecture (D-LSP1=C): a demand-driven incremental query engine — inputs (file text, module graph roots) and derived queries (tokens-of-file, ast-of-file, module-graph, types-of-item, diagnostics-of-file, symbols-of-file, callers-of-item), each memoized with precise dependency tracking and a global revision counter. jet check, jet dev, the REPL, and jet lsp become clients of the same engine, so editor answers can never disagree with the compiler. jet-semindex's ratified query API (D-SEMINDEX1) is the persistence/format layer, fed by the engine instead of batch runs.

Build order:
1. Engine core: new crate crates/jet-queries (std-only). Query trait + memo table + dependency edges + revision invalidation. Wrap existing lexer/parser/sema entry points as queries without changing their internals (I3). Unit tests: edit one file of a 3-file project, prove only dependent queries recompute (counter assertions).
2. LSP on the engine: rewrite Source/LSP/Check.rs request paths to engine queries; keep the JSON/protocol layer. Differential gate: LSP publishDiagnostics byte-identical to `jet check --json` for every tests/ui fixture (new tests/lsp differential test — this is the no-two-brains exit).
3. Incremental sync: textDocumentSync 2 (range edits) in Server.rs + rope-or-line-table doc storage in Position.rs. Latency test: single-keystroke edit on a 2,000-line fixture re-checks in <10ms warm (test with counters, not wall-clock flake; a wall-clock smoke stays #[ignore] for local runs).
4. Wave 1 — beginner-critical (ships before anything else user-visible): signatureHelp (trigger '(' and ','; params + doc comment from AST), documentSymbol (nested outline: fns, structs+methods, enums, traits, modules), completion quality pass (labels get type signatures; keyword completions context-filtered).
5. Wave 2 — navigation: workspaceSymbol (engine project view), foldingRange (blocks, comments, use-groups), documentHighlight (occurrences via resolution, read vs write kinds — v5 & writes light differently), selectionRange (AST-walk expand).
6. Wave 3 — power: completion auto-import (insert `use` on commit) + snippet support (fn call parens, .{ } constructor), prepareRename (reject keywords/foreign symbols with Jet-voiced message), semanticTokens range + delta (keep full as fallback), inlayHint refinements (param names at call sites, off-by-default toggle).
7. Wave 4 — hierarchy + long tail: callHierarchy (incoming/outgoing via callers-of-item query), typeHierarchy (impl/trait relations), documentLink (use-paths + doc URLs), codeLens (run/test lens over #Test fns, off by default). Advertise only what ships: initialize_response in Server.rs grows per wave, never ahead of tests.
8. Engine serves the CLI: `jet check` and `jet dev` reuse the warm engine in watch/daemon mode (D-DEV4 loop); differential battery from E2-M4 must stay green (interpreter parity untouched).

Exit criteria (all must hold — no partial done):
- Every capability advertised in initialize_response has a passing test in tests/lsp.rs (capability-coverage meta-test enumerates the JSON and fails on untested ones).
- Differential gate (stage 2) green across all ui fixtures.
- Incremental-recompute unit proofs green; keystroke path does not re-run whole-file sema when edit is local to one item.
- tests/lsp/, tests/dev.rs, tests/repl.rs, full suite green.
- docs: editors/vscode/README.md + editors/zed/README.md feature tables updated; architecture.md gains the query-engine section (R-rules untouched).

Gates: none open — D-LSP1/D-LSP2 ratified 2026-07-05. Log both in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md tooling section during stage 1 commit.

Delegation: stages 1–3 sequential (one agent, non-isolated — worktree agents branch stale bases); waves 4–7 parallelizable per-feature after stage 3 lands. sonnet for feature waves, opus for stage 1 engine design review before code.
