cards.title: Highlighting: one source of truth across editors
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: three hand-kept grammars drift — vscode tmLanguage 164 lines, tree-sitter 998, zed highlights.scm 136, vs 569 registered tokens in Syntax.rs (I7). The v5 'copy' verb (shipped S4) is highlighted in NO grammar; VS Code, Zed, and GitHub color the same file differently. Owner: 'even code highlighting doesnt seem consistent.' Decision D-HL1.
cards.plan:
Highlighting single source of truth under D-HL1=D (grammars generated from Syntax.rs + LSP semantic-token overlay, CI drift gate). Implement on master. Invariant I7: Syntax.rs is already the registry every user-typeable token must live in — this card makes that fact enforce coloring.

Build order:
1. Classify the registry: extend crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs entries with a highlight class per token (keyword.control / keyword.declaration / keyword.ownership / marker / operator / sigil / literal-prefix ...). Mechanical: a const table or attribute alongside each existing entry; no token strings move. Any token without a class = compile error in the generator, so future ratifications can't skip it.
2. Generator: `jet devtools grammars` in Source/CmdDevTools.rs. Emits BEGIN/END GENERATED sections inside: editors/vscode/syntaxes/jet.tmLanguage.json (keyword/marker/operator patterns), editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js keyword externals (or a generated keywords.js the grammar requires), editors/zed/languages/jet/highlights.scm keyword block. Hand-written structure rules (strings, comments, interpolation, blocks) stay outside the markers and are preserved byte-for-byte on regeneration. Generator is deterministic (sorted output) so regeneration is diff-stable.
3. Drift gate: tests/grammar.rs gains every_syntax_token_is_highlighted — for each user-typeable token in Syntax.rs, assert presence in each grammar's generated section, and assert the generated sections match a fresh in-memory generation (stale-file detection). Red today (copy, ^, & missing) until stage 2 output is committed. This test joins the CI PR gate (#211).
4. Semantic overlay: extend Source/LSP semantic tokens — add token types/modifiers for v5 ownership (& write-borrow, ^ move, copy verb), markers (#Test/#Unsafe/... as decorator-class), retired/foreign keywords (E03xx teaching-error spellings) explicitly NOT keyword-colored. editors/vscode/package.json semanticTokenScopes maps the new types; zed extension.toml equivalents. Fixture test: canon.jet + examples/features/memory/ownership.jet token dumps snapshot-tested in tests/lsp.rs.
5. Regenerate all three grammars, run editors/*/install.sh locally, verify canon.jet renders consistently in VS Code + Zed; screenshot pair in the card log. GitHub rendering uses the committed tmLanguage — verified by the drift test alone.
6. Docs: editors/README pointers; note in syntax-decisions.md tooling section (D-HL1=D logged); CLAUDE.md syntax-decision protocol gains one line: 'ratifying syntax = run jet devtools grammars, commit regenerated sections' (the drift test makes forgetting red anyway).

Exit criteria:
- cargo test --test grammar green, including staleness check.
- Semantic-token snapshots green for canon.jet + ownership.jet + copy_verb.jet.
- `copy`, `^`, `&`, and every S75/S76/v5 token colored in all three grammars; retired spellings (val, var, dotless construction) not keyword-colored anywhere.
- Full suite green; zed grammar-repo stays untracked (build artifact — .gitignore already covers it).

Gates: none — D-HL1 ratified 2026-07-05. No new user-typeable syntax, so no formatter work.

Delegation: stages 1–2 one sonnet agent (single subsystem); stage 4 separate agent after 2 lands; stage 3 test written FIRST (red) per workflow loop.

cards.title: CI and quality gates — the professional bar
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: CI runs 5 of ~70 test targets (lib, truthfulness, diagnostic_snapshots, golden, cross) — lsp, fmt, repl, jetpack, workspace, web_build, ownership etc. never run on PR. CI also still calls frozen tools/Tower/Tower.mjs (MOVED.md says don't). No clippy/rustfmt/warning gate; no perf-regression or fuzz cadence. Decisions: D-CI1 gate composition, D-CI2 warning policy.
cards.plan:
CI + quality gates under D-CI1=A (full suite sharded on every PR; nightly perf/fuzz/coverage/multi-OS) and D-CI2=A (zero-warning gate with card-referenced #[expect]). Implement on master.

Build order:
1. Warning sweep first (D-CI2): fix or #[expect(lint, reason = "#<card>: <why>")] every current warning across the workspace. Known: scrutinee_bool in crates/jet-jit/src/lib.rs:1916 gets #[expect(dead_code, reason = "#125: JIT tier-1a scrutinee lowering, wired in next stage")]. Rule goes in CLAUDE.md style section: dead code without a card-referenced expect is deletable on sight; expects self-expire (unfulfilled-expectation errors when the code goes live).
2. Lint config: [workspace.lints] in root Cargo.toml — rust.warnings = deny in CI (via RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings in the workflow, not in the manifest, so local iteration stays friendly); clippy correctness+suspicious groups on, style/pedantic off (house conventions win). rustfmt.toml matching current formatting (verify `cargo fmt --check` is near-clean first; if a one-time format commit is needed it is its own mechanical commit, no logic changes).
3. Shard the suite: 4 PR jobs with an explicit shard map (a checked-in list, e.g. tools/ci/shards.toml): shard-1 front-end (lexer/parser/fmt/grammar/ui/ui_lint/syntax_reconciliation...), shard-2 sema (ownership/generics/effects/typestate/pure/taint...), shard-3 codegen+examples (golden/canon/cross/corelib/release_gates...), shard-4 tooling (lsp/repl/debug/dev/jetpack/pkg/workspace/web_*/observe/cli...). Meta-test tools/ci/shards-complete (or tests/ci_shards.rs): every tests/*.rs file assigned to exactly one shard, fails on unassigned new files — no silent coverage loss, ever.
4. Rewrite .github/workflows/ci.yml: keep nix toolchain job skeleton; PR = build + 4 shard jobs (nix develop -c cargo test --test <list>) + cargo fmt --check + clippy + tower status via NEW path (node Tower/tower.mjs status — the frozen tools/Tower/Tower.mjs step dies) + aarch64 QEMU smoke as today. Cache /nix and cargo target dir keyed on flake.lock+Cargo.lock so shard wall-clock stays near today's.
5. Nightly workflow (.github/workflows/nightly.yml): full suite on ubuntu + macos; perf ratchet via tools/perf/ci-perf-check.sh against tools/perf/baseline.json (regression = red + auto card via tower CLI); fuzz cadence — run tests/fuzz_sema.rs in extended mode (env-gated iteration count) 30 min; coverage report (nix devshell tool; CI-side only, not a compiler dep — I6 untouched) published as artifact with a ratchet floor once a baseline exists.
6. Failure→card automation: nightly failure step runs `node Tower/tower.mjs card add --kind bug ...` with the failing job link (guard against duplicates by title search first).
7. Canary proof: after everything lands, a deliberate throwaway PR breaking a previously-unrun target (e.g. tests/repl.rs) must go red; record the run link on this card, then close the canary.

cards.title: HTTPS by default in core.http
cards.body: core.net/core.http default build is plain-HTTP; https needs opt-in core.tls (jet-net: 'HTTPS requires a TLS feature; the default build is HTTP-only'). Nearly every real API is https — first-week beginners hit this wall. Decision D-TLS1: how TLS becomes default (vendored rustls bridge -> native post-E3, system TLS, or status quo).
cards.plan:
HTTPS by default under D-TLS1=A: rustls in the default build via the I6 FFI-bridge pattern, certificate verification pinned to system trust roots, native Jet TLS post-E3 only behind an external security-audit gate. Implement on master. Invariants: I2 (every TLS failure is a Jet-voiced diagnostic — rustls/OS error text never reaches the user raw), I4 (every new diagnostic gets a code + what/why/fix + ui snapshot), I6 (rustls rides the bridge like wasmtime/age precedents — D-DEP-CRYPTO1 governance, not a compiler dep).

Build order:
1. jet-net grows a default-on TLS path: rustls + system trust roots (rustls-native-certs-class) behind the existing fetch API in crates/jet-net; ureq's tls feature wired accordingly. Default build = https works; a no-tls build flag remains for freestanding/size-gated targets (release_gates.rs budgets re-checked — if the size budget breaks, that goes back to the owner as a question, not a silent budget bump).
2. core.http / core.net client: https URLs work in `jet run` with zero manifest. The E-code path 'https needs core.tls' dies for the client; core.tls package remains for advanced config (pinning, client certs, custom roots) per option A's decided scope.
3. Server side: extend the #17 HTTP server surface with TLS serving — API shape follows the existing ratified server surface (.tls(cert, key) style continuation of the #17 mandate; if the shape needs anything beyond a method on the existing builder, STOP and ballot it — do not invent surface).
4. Diagnostics (product copy, snapshot-pinned): new E42xx family — certificate invalid/expired/hostname mismatch, handshake failure, no trust roots found (the minimal-container case: name the fix — install ca-certificates), protocol errors. Each: docs/spec/diagnostics.md entry, jet explain page, tests/ui snapshot. The front end translates every rustls error class; an untranslated class panicking through = P0 per I2.
5. Tests without network: local test server with self-signed + valid-chain fixtures under tests/fixtures (generate once, check in; regeneration script documented); happy-path https fetch, each E42xx provoked deliberately. CI never touches the internet.
6. Example: examples/features/net/https_fetch.jet against the fixture server (env-pointed base URL so the example text reads like the real world but the test stays hermetic); golden-tested (I5).
7. Record the security gate: release-policy.md gains the D-TLS1 clause — native-TLS may replace rustls as default only after external audit + interop battery (vs rustls and OpenSSL test vectors); syntax-decisions.md logs D-TLS1=A in the stdlib section; roadmap.md deferred-registry paragraph updated (TLS line now says https default via rustls bridge).

Exit criteria:
- Fresh clone, default build: https fetch example runs (fixture server) — no package, no manifest.
- All E42xx snapshots green; jet explain covers each; diagnostics_coverage.rs enforced.
- Freestanding/size budgets green or explicitly re-balloted.
- core.tls advanced path still works (its existing tests stay green).
- Full suite green; docs (release-policy, syntax-decisions, roadmap, core-library.md) updated in the same series.

cards.body: Update jetpack run package to show clearly that a package is running/was run. When running cowsay with no input args, looked like jetpack shell was frozen

#215 plan: make jetpack run package visibility obvious

Decision: no owner decision needed. Owner reported that running cowsay with no input args looked like a frozen jetpack shell. This is output/UX polish inside existing run-package behavior, not new syntax.

Build order:
1. Identify explicit package-run path in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/CLI.rs cmd_run. Today explicit ref plus no -- command falls through to Shell::enter, which can look frozen. Keep project-env run with no explicit ref as shell entry, but for explicit package refs run the package binary by default or print an unmistakable banner before shell entry. Preferred: explicit jetpack run nixpkgs:cowsay with no -- runs cowsay, matching top-level jet run lowering.

4. Top-level parity: Source/main.rs dispatch_nixpkgs_run lowers jet run nixpkgs:<tool> to jetpack run nixpkgs:<tool> -- <tool>. Ensure visibility appears for direct jetpack run and top-level jet run without duplicate status.

cards.title: Bootstrap readiness gate: dogfood portfolio + memory-model soundness campaign
cards.body:
HARD GATE for e8 — no port work starts until this card is done and owner signs off. Core lang must be locked-happy (stdlib may still flux).

Evidence required:
1. **Dogfood portfolio** — enough real example projects in Jet, chosen for fringe needs and complexity, to stress the language end-to-end: compiler-shaped programs (formatter port, interpreter, arena/index-handle AST work), long-lived concurrent services, comptime-heavy code, FFI-heavy code, large multi-package workspaces. Each project reviewed for (a) readability and (b) how well an agent/human can reason about the codebase cold.
2. **Memory-model soundness campaign** — adversarial stress of memory model v5 (D-MEM1: bare/read, &/write, ^/take, second-class borrows) to Rust-borrow-checker confidence: soundness test suite, fuzzing, differential testing vs rustc on generated code, deliberate escape attempts (use-after-take, aliasing writes, arena dangling-index patterns), and I1 audit that no safe-Jet program can reach UB. Exit = virtually 100% certainty it is as solid as Rust.
3. **Syntax/coverage sweep** — every ratified surface feature exercised in the portfolio; gaps become examples or ballots.
4. **Owner sign-off ballot** — final "core lang is frozen enough to port" decision, minted when evidence is assembled.

Blocks the full-port card.

cards.title: Full port: self-host the Jet compiler in Jet
cards.body:
Tracks the entire bootstrap arc. Gated by the readiness card (blockedBy) — do not start before it is done and owner-signed.

Owner gates to mint as ballots when e8 opens:
- **D-SELFHOST1 charter** — port scope: (A) rewrite in Jet, keep emitting Rust + hidden rustc backend; (B) native backend first, rustc leaves the bootstrap chain; (C) piecewise, one crate at a time via C-ABI linking into the Rust driver.
- **I6 restatement** — zero-external-deps invariant re-expressed for Jet compiler source + what stage0 may be (pinned Rust-built release binary).
- **I2 fate** — if the Jet compiler still emits Rust, bootstrap forever needs a Rust toolchain; owner accepts or demands the native backend first.

Mechanics:
- Stage discipline: stage0 = pinned Rust-built jet; stage1 = jet compiled by stage0; stage2 = jet compiled by stage1; exit test = stage1 ≡ stage2 byte-identical. Requires deterministic codegen (no hash-order leaks, no timestamps).
- Feature-freeze line: self-hosted compiler uses only the Jet subset stage0 supports; lint against drift.
- Test-harness parity: golden tests, tests/ui snapshots, tests/decisions.rs run unchanged against the Jet-built binary.
- Subsystem inventory to scope per-ballot: lexer, parser, sema (incl. memory model v5 checker), codegen, comptime tier-0 interpreter, JIT tier (see #10/#11 — Cranelift cannot port; own VM/JIT cards own that), jet fmt, LSP, jet debug, jetpack driver. Some may stay Rust indefinitely — charter decides.
- Cheapest credible first step once unblocked: port the lexer, link into the Rust driver via C ABI, run the full suite — generates the real gap list.

cards.title: Ship bootable jetos VM installer and install/reboot proof
cards.body: Owner acceptance: run a VM, install jetos, reboot into installed jetos, and prove it works as a real OS. Implement real QEMU boot media/disk image flow, installer environment, disk partition/format/install, bootloader or equivalent boot path, first boot into installed generation, guest-side verification, and reproducible harness. Done means a command produces media, QEMU boots it, installs to a virtual disk, reboots from that disk, then verifies packages, services, networking, generations, rollback, and proof artifacts inside the guest. The current jetos-installer-<host>.img proof text is not sufficient.
cards.plan: jetos-vm-installer

log.text: DECREE AUDIT: installer/QEMU install+reboot machinery real and keeps; caveat — kernel/initrd came from the host borrow, to be replaced by e7 #716.

Closed bootable JetOS VM installer/install-reboot proof: installer media boots into /jetos/init, writes GPT + ESP + jetos-root, copies generation closure, installs Limine config, powers down, then QEMU boots the installed disk via firmware with no direct kernel/initrd/append. Graphical proof still direct-boots verifier overlay for VNC/stdvga and checks desktop launchers. Verification: nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack; real JETOS_CACHYOS_* jetos os vm prove halcyon; nix develop -c cargo test; nix develop -c cargo fmt --check.

Real QEMU proof: JETPACK_ROOT=/tmp/jetos-real-qemu-root-62 JETOS_CACHYOS_KERNEL=/run/current-system/kernel JETOS_CACHYOS_INITRD=/run/current-system/initrd JETOS_CACHYOS_MODULES=/nix/store/0ibb5fi1cpl5asqhy1x1n2hc48nnpnnk-linux-cachyos-latest-7.0.11-modules/lib/modules/7.0.11-cachyos target/debug/jetos os vm prove halcyon --disk /tmp/jetos-real-qemu-62.qcow2 --name esp-smoke --offline => guest-passed. Logs show boot-installer installed to /dev/sda, boot-installed-disk booted OVMF hard disk + Limine and mounted installed root, graphical verifier saw fb0/fbcon and emitted desktop-launchers-run. cards.title: corelib audit: core.files/core.path — file I/O parity with pathlib/Go os/Rust fs
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python pathlib ergonomics, Go os robustness, Rust std::fs safety. Card #58 (path objects, atomic write, dir-walk) is done — first verify what actually shipped vs docs/reference/core-library.md (the doc shows no walk/glob/metadata), then close the residual gaps so core.files is a strict superset of the bar.

Gaps to audit and close: file metadata (size, mtime, created, permissions, file type) as a typed Stat value; create_dir_all / remove_dir / remove_all; glob patterns and recursive walk with entry filtering; symlink create/read/detect and hardlinks; temp files and temp dirs with RAII cleanup; atomic write (verify #58); advisory file locking; canonicalize/absolute; copy_dir tree; seek/offset reads and byte-stream (non-line) buffered readers/writers; fsync/flush-to-disk; filesystem watch (notify events) — watch may deserve its own module name (ballot).

Done means: every gap either ships with example + golden test, or is recorded as an owner-declined non-goal in the stdlib map. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan:
Acceptance: core.files/core.path must beat Python pathlib, Go os/filepath, and Rust std::fs for ordinary scripting/build-tool work, while preserving Jet's one-path, safe-default, audit-friendly model.

Current facts found during plan pass:
- docs/reference/core-library.md currently documents core.files as string-path helpers plus open/create/append streaming handles.
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md records D-PATHFS1 typed Path (from/join/parent/extension/stem/write_atomic/walk) but still labels part of it unbuilt; code already contains Path TIR/prelude/sema hooks, so implementation must verify shipped behavior and fix docs drift.
- D-FSWATCH1 is ratified as files.watch, with owner comment: include processes and ports now, not later. That requires a shared watch/event model, not only a filesystem helper.

Gates queued:
- D-FSOPS1: exact deep filesystem/path operation surface and Path-vs-String model.
- D-WATCH-SCOPE1: exact watch composition surface for files, process exit, and port readiness.

Implementation plan after gates clear:
1. Verification baseline: add/confirm focused tests for currently claimed Path API (Path.from, join, parent, extension, stem, write_atomic, walk), existing core.files helpers, and docs/API-freeze snapshots. Fix any docs/code mismatch before adding new surface.
2. Data model: add typed Stat, FileKind, WalkEntry, TempFile/TempDir RAII handles, FileLock, WatchHandle, WatchEvent, WatchSet. Keep IOError product-copy shape; add diagnostics only for sema-visible misuse.
3. Sema/API surface: register ratified functions/methods in CheckerCoreLib known-items, effect caps, target-profile availability, comptime impurity policy where relevant, and semantic-index/docs facts.
4. Runtime/codegen: lower through TIR/prelude only; no codegen checks. Implement std-only filesystem ops first; platform-specific gaps become typed IOError variants or documented unsupported cases, never raw OS errors.
5. Watch: implement debounced files.watch plus process/port watchers per ratified D-WATCH-SCOPE1. If a native OS watcher cannot be std-only on a platform, use the existing FFI-bridge dependency posture only after owner-approved dependency gate; otherwise ship a polling fallback only if the ballot allows it and report its fidelity in WatchEvent facts.
6. Examples/goldens: publish_files.jet exercises create_dir_all, walk, stat, copy_dir, write_atomic, temp_dir cleanup; dev_runner_watch.jet exercises files/process/port watch without shell polling. Golden tests pin output; focused Rust tests cover edge cases.
7. Docs: update docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/spec.md effect table, syntax-decisions D-PATHFS1/D-FSOPS1/D-WATCH-SCOPE1 entries, and stdlib gap ledger (#310 if present).
8. Verification: targeted tests for corelib/golden/dev/watch paths, then nix develop -c cargo build, hello.jet smoke, relevant examples, and final nix develop -c cargo test before closing.

Devil-pass hardening:
- Avoid two mechanisms: every string path entrypoint coerces to Path before audit/effects/codegen see it.
- Avoid shell-shaped footguns: no blessed mkdir/cp/rm subprocess workaround remains in docs.
- Avoid watch taxonomy sprawl: domain constructors return one shared event/watch abstraction.
- Avoid silent platform drift: watch/stat/symlink fidelity is test-pinned or exposed as typed capability facts.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.process — subprocess parity with Python subprocess/Go os/exec
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python subprocess flexibility, Go os/exec explicitness, duct-style pipelines. Current: run([cmd]) capturing everything + exit(code) only.

Gaps: streaming stdin write and incremental stdout/stderr read while the child runs; env control (set, remove, clear-then-set); working-directory control; timeout with kill; send signals (terminate/kill/interrupt); detached spawn; exit status detail (signal vs code); pipelines (child stdout → child stdin) without a shell; safe argv-only execution documented (no shell interpolation footgun — safe by default); output size limits; inherit-vs-capture per stream.

Done means: a build-tool-shaped example (spawn, stream logs live, timeout, propagate exit) ships with golden output. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan:
Acceptance: core.process must cover real build-tool and agent-operation workflows without shell strings: safe argv-only execution by default, streaming logs, exact exit status, env/cwd control, timeouts, signals, detached children, output limits, and shell-free pipelines.

Current facts found during plan pass:
- docs/reference/core-library.md documents only process.exit(code) and process.run([String]) -> ProcessResult ? IOError.
- ProcessResult currently has code/output/errors only.
- Sema/codegen know core.process exit/run only; effects classify core.process as Exec.
- Existing taint tests treat process.run as an Exec sink; any expanded surface must keep that policy coverage.

Gate queued:
- D-PROCESS1: exact process spawning/pipeline surface.

Implementation plan after gate clears:
1. Baseline tests: pin current process.run/exit behavior and taint Exec-sink coverage before expanding.
2. Data model: add ProcessSpec, Child, ExitStatus, StreamMode, ProcessPipe/Pipeline types per ratified surface. Keep argv lists canonical; no shell-string helper unless separately ratified.
3. Sema/effects: register all new calls in CheckerCoreLib known-items, mark Exec effects, preserve taint sink checks on every execution path, and type-check stream/stdin/stdout modes.
4. Runtime/codegen: implement through TIR/prelude only; no codegen checks. Use std::process Command internally; map OS errors into IOError and child outcomes into ExitStatus without exposing Rust/stdout internals.
5. Safety defaults: bounded capture default or explicit output_limit, no inherited env mutation, timeout kill semantics documented, process handles RAII-clean where possible, and interrupt/terminate/kill behavior platform-pinned.
6. Examples/goldens: build_runner.jet streams stdout, sets cwd/env, times out a child, pipelines two argv commands, propagates exit. Keep fixture commands cross-platform or test-gated.
7. Docs: update docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/spec.md effects table, syntax-decisions D-PROCESS1 entry, and stdlib ledger (#310 if present).
8. Verification: targeted process/taint/golden tests, cargo build, hello smoke, process example smoke, final nix develop -c cargo test before close.

Devil-pass hardening:
- No shell string default; argv-only is the safe path.
- No silent output buffering footgun; streaming and capture limits are explicit.
- No second process model; process.run lowers to ProcessSpec.run.
- No raw OS status leaks; ExitStatus is typed and portable.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.env + system facts — os info, signals, process identity
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go os/runtime + Python os/platform/signal. Current core.env: get/set/current_dir/home_dir.

cards.title: jetos: declarative VM integration-test framework (NixOS test-driver parity)
cards.body:
The NixOS VM test framework is its most-lauded infrastructure — jetos needs a better one to claim drop-in-and-better. Scope: declare a multi-host scenario in Jet (system.<host> configs + a typed test script — not strings driving Python like NixOS), orchestrate QEMU guests from the #263 harness, typed assertions (unit active, port open, file content, command output), inter-VM networking, deterministic replay + proof artifacts, failure output in Jet's diagnostic voice.

Beat-NixOS axes: typed test script with sema-checked host/service references (a typo'd service name fails at compile time), and first-class artifact/provenance capture. Builds on #262/#263 — coordinate with the jetos agent; this is a new layer, not their installer/system-core scope.
cards.plan:
Plan refreshed 2026-07-07 by codex-main.

Ratified decisions:
- D-JOS-VMTEST1=A: Hybrid: vmtest declarations as test targets. Top-level vmtest.<name> declarations are the canonical scenario surface, and the same object is also a normal test target for CI, filtering, artifacts, and package integration. Single-host smoke tests can be authored as shorthand that expands to vmtest; multi-host topology stays explicit. Beginners run one command; experts control host graph, network, replay, timeout, artifacts, and proof capture.
- D-JOS-VMASSERT1=A: Hybrid: typed host handles plus declarative check values. The test body uses typed host handles and assertion methods. Those methods also produce declarative check values/proof facts, so Studio/CI can render and replay them. Common checks stay one-line and type-checked; experts can write ordinary Jet control flow around them. String shell commands remain an explicit fallback assertion, never the default.

cards.title: jetos: fleet/remote deployment — push generations with proof-gated rollback
cards.body:
deploy-rs/colmena/NixOps parity, first-party. Roadmap already names fleet rollout as future Epoch 7 — this card tracks it. Scope: build closures locally (or on a builder), push to remote hosts over SSH, activate with proof-before-switch (#236) on the remote, health-check window with automatic rollback, multi-host rollout ordering with dependency graph, secrets delivery at deploy time, no daemon/root beyond what activation needs (U28), offline-capable (U29). Reconcile with U15 (fleet parse/capture, done) for the config side.

Beat-NixOS axes: proof-gated activation per host and typed rollout plans with explainable failure. Coordinate with jetos agent; blocked conceptually on #262's activation contract.

Plan refreshed 2026-07-07 by codex-main.

Ratified decisions:
- D-JOS-FLEETTARGET1=A: Hybrid: host target fields with label defaults and reusable target refs. Each fleet host carries typed target/authority fields beside its system. If omitted, the friendly label can be used as a safe SSH default. Reusable deploy.target refs avoid duplication for bastions/CI. Host key policy, privilege boundary, and identity are proof-visible.
- D-JOS-FLEETROLLOUT1=A: Hybrid: staged proof-gated rollout with plan/stage controls. Default push is staged and proof-gated with rollback-and-stop. Experts can choose batch/canary/dependency order, health timeout, and stage-only/continue flows using the same rollout object. All-at-once is an explicit policy, never the default.

Ready state: Owner gates clear; card remains dependency-blocked by #262 until that card verifies.

Acceptance: jetos fleet deploy must replace deploy-rs/colmena/NixOps for ordinary fleets: typed fleet declarations, explicit remote authority, local or builder closure build, SSH push, remote proof-before-switch, health window, automatic rollback, multi-host order, secrets delivery, and replayable artifacts.

Existing ratified base:
- D-JPK-FLEET1: module fleet.<name> and jet push <fleet>.

1. Extend FleetPlan from hosts-only capture to ratified target/auth and rollout fields; preserve E1242 host-system cross-checks and replace E1243 gated notice.
2. Build phase: realize each host's system generation through #262, apply host overrides, record per-host closure/provenance/tool hashes.

4. Remote activation: run proof-before-switch remotely with minimal privilege, write remote generation ledger, stream structured logs, and never expose raw SSH/QEMU output as the primary diagnostic.
5. Health/rollback: implement ratified staged policy, per-host health checks, automatic rollback, halted rollout state, and resume/replay metadata.
6. Secrets: integrate U13 recipients and deliver secrets at deploy time only to selected host identities.
7. Tests: fake SSH transport tests for build/ship/activate/rollback, bad target diagnostics, unknown host still E1242, and a local loopback smoke where possible.
8. Artifacts/docs: systems/fleets/<name>/proof.json, per-host logs, rollout graph, docs/spec + diagnostics updates.

cards.title: jetos acceptance fixture: recreate the owner's ~/nixos 100% in jetos
cards.body:
The concrete dogfood proof that jetos is a drop-in NixOS replacement: the owner's real ~/nixos flake, recreated fully in jetos declarations, building and VM-boot-proving a halcyon-equivalent system.

Coverage matrix (config feature → covering card):
- flake inputs/pins/channels, per-host channel swap → jetpack U21/U30 + overlays card
- overlays/patches, NUR, allowUnfree → jetpack overlays card
- multi-variant hosts (halcyon / halcyon-plasma-beta: mkForce DM swap, tags, channel override) → module-priorities card + #326 specialisations
- disko input, btrfs → #328 declarative disks
- limine + kernel profiles + zram + sysctl + scx → kernel-tuning card (D-JOS-BOOTKERNEL1/KERNELSRC1 ratified)
- users/groups, networking (hostname, NetworkManager, nameservers, firewall ports), security (sudo, rtkit) → #262
- home-manager + per-app modules (git/ssh/fish/starship/ghostty/helix/vscode+cursor extensions/nixcord/spicetify/browsers/…) → #321 + app-module-library card
- plasma-manager/dconf-class DE settings, KDE beside GNOME default, audio, localization, xdg-mimes, fonts, virtualization (libvirt/spice), gaming (steam/wine/gamemode), smartcard → desktop-breadth card
- stylix (wallpaper/palette/fonts/cursor) → theming card
- flatpak reconcile + appimage → flatpak card
- custom ISO host → #263
- substituters → jetpack cache/providers (shipped)
- secrets → U13/#262
- jetlang packaged from local path → jetpack path providers

Exit criteria: every module file under ~/nixos has a jetos equivalent expressed in ratified syntax; the config builds; the VM test framework (#320) boots it and passes desktop-session + app-presence assertions; a written diff of anything deliberately not recreated, owner-acknowledged. cards.title: Sema soundness audit: adversarial review + fuzz corpus expansion
cards.body:
jet-sema (~40k lines) owns all checking (I3); a soundness hole means unsound generated Rust reaches users silently — the worst bug class in the project (I1/I2). #185 (done) swept reachable ICEs and rustc leaks; this card hunts the other two classes: accepts-invalid (sema approves a program it must reject) and miscompiles (approved program computes the wrong thing).

Audit surface, in priority order:
1. Ownership/move/borrow proofs, including the tier-2 view/ref rules (E2-M5) and RAII cleanup (S63).
2. Sendability proofs for tasks/channels (E2-M1) — data-race freedom claims.
3. #Unsafe gate containment (D-LL1): generated `unsafe` appears only inside user-written gates; safe Jet emits none (tests/golden.rs enforces — extend it).
4. Generics + trait resolution: associated types, error conversion for `?`, trait delegation (S62), argument labels/defaults (S61).
5. Comptime/@Pure evaluation boundary (M9.5, E2-M16) — comptime results must agree with runtime semantics.
6. Newer surface: fan-out `f.[…]` (S75), fixed-size lists `[T#N]` (S76), refinements (D-REFINE1 when landed).

Method: adversarial review pass per area → each suspected hole becomes a tests/ui fixture or golden test BEFORE the fix; extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs with generative/mutation strategies over the ratified grammar; use the interpreter-vs-compiled differential battery (I2, jet dev parity) as a miscompile oracle — divergence is always a bug in one side.

Done means: audit notes committed under docs/ (findings, per-area verdict, corpus description); every confirmed hole has a failing test then a fix, all suite green; fuzz corpus + runner wired so #211 CI can execute it in budget; no invariant bent. No owner gates expected — if a finding requires a semantics change visible to users, ballot it before fixing.
cards.plan: Order: (1) read docs/spec/architecture.md R1–R12 + spec.md sections per area; (2) per audit area, spawn adversarial review (opus-tier reasoning) over the relevant sema modules — CheckerCore.rs, CheckerInfer/, CheckerCoreLib.rs, Bundle.rs; (3) write attack programs as tests/ui fixtures — expect reject; write miscompile candidates as differential fixtures — expect byte-identical interpreter/compiled output; (4) extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs: grammar-directed generation from crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs so the fuzzer only speaks ratified syntax; (5) fix confirmed holes smallest-first, full suite between fixes; (6) audit notes + corpus docs; full nix develop -c cargo test green at close.

cards.title: Workspace re-partition: shrink jet-driver, make placeholder crates real or fold them
cards.body:
jet-driver is ~44k lines and has absorbed three products: the compiler driver, Jetpack (Jetpack/CLI.rs ~4.5k, package engine), and JetOS (Jetpack/JetOS.rs ~7.2k). Meanwhile four workspace crates are shells: jet-queries (375 lines), jet-rt (401), jet-net (295), jet-impact (314). Epoch 4 (jetpack) and Epoch 7 (jetos) will grow these surfaces substantially — re-partition before they grow, not after.

Scope:
1. Extract Jetpack and JetOS out of jet-driver into their own crates (jet-pack / jet-os or per ratified naming canon: jetpack engine, jetos). jet-driver keeps only compile-pipeline orchestration + CLI dispatch.
2. For each shell crate decide: become real now, or fold into its owner until needed. jet-queries is the big one — it is the incremental-compilation seam; decide whether the query architecture becomes load-bearing now (retrofitting incrementality into a 268k-line compiler later is strictly worse). Produce a recommendation with the decision reasoning recorded in architecture.md.
3. Update docs/spec/architecture.md: crate map, dependency direction rules, which crate owns which pipeline stage (R1–R12 mapping).
4. Enforce direction: no back-edges (e.g. codegen must not depend on driver). Add a workspace-level check if cheap (cargo tree assertions in a test).

cards.body:
Largest files today: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib.rs (13.5k lines), Source/Canvas.rs (8.4k), crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower.rs (8.3k), crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib.rs (7.5k), crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/JetOS.rs (7.2k), Parser/Items.rs (5.7k), TIR/emit.rs (5.3k), TIR/subset.rs (5.1k), CheckerInfer/calls.rs (4.8k), Jetpack/CLI.rs (4.5k), jet-jit/src/lib.rs (4.5k). These files burn agent context every session and are where merge mistakes concentrate. Style rule already says small modules — enforce it.

Scope: semantics-preserving decomposition of every file above ~3k lines into responsibility-named submodules. Seams follow responsibility, not line count — e.g. CoreLib.rs splits by core module family (files/io/net/…), lower.rs by TIR construct family, CheckerCoreLib.rs mirroring the CoreLib split so sema and codegen stay navigable in parallel. Target ≤ ~1,500 lines per file; judgment allowed where a real unit resists splitting — record why in the commit message.

Rules: pure code motion — no renames of public items, no behavior change, no drive-by refactors. Safety net is the existing suite: golden outputs and UI snapshots must be byte-identical; full suite green after every file's decomposition (one file per commit). Sequencing: JetOS.rs, CLI.rs, and Canvas.rs only AFTER the workspace re-partition card lands, so they move across crates once, not twice; start with CoreLib.rs / lower.rs / CheckerCoreLib.rs / Items.rs, which the re-partition does not touch.

Done means: no source file above the target without a recorded justification; module maps make sense from names alone; zero snapshot diffs; full nix develop -c cargo test green. No owner gates.
cards.plan: Order: (1) CoreLib.rs — split by core.* family, mod.rs keeps the registration table; (2) CheckerCoreLib.rs — mirror the same family split; (3) TIR lower.rs then emit.rs then subset.rs — split by construct family (items, exprs, patterns, control flow, closures, tasks); (4) Parser/Items.rs + CheckerInfer/calls.rs; (5) jet-jit/src/lib.rs; (6) wait for re-partition card, then JetOS.rs, Jetpack/CLI.rs, Canvas.rs inside their new homes. cards.title: Canvas frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified Canvas frontend redesign as the next E6 Canvas slice. Build the modified hybrid surface: Workbench-style project/file viewer, hybrid code/split/graph editor, context-command model, UE5-style node/pin visual language, hover-only types, compact getter capsules, embedded simple variables, graphite styling, and detail toggles. Source remains the only semantic truth.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas modified hybrid UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CANVAS1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- Existing E6 Canvas architecture and protocol from #352; do not introduce a graph asset or GUI-owned semantics.

Scope:
- Source/Canvas/html.rs, Source/Canvas/js.rs, Source/Canvas/*.rs protocol helpers, tests/canvas.rs, tests/web_dev.rs, docs/design/frontends/canvas/NOTES.md if behavior notes drift.
- Keep /canvas and /__jet_canvas routes source-backed.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace the old palette-first left surface with a persistent Workbench-style project/file viewer backed by /canvas/project and source ids. It must show workspace/package/file/function graph navigation and source-control/provenance facts where available.
2. Keep hybrid editor modes: Code, Split, Graph. Ensure selection, source-span jump, graph picker, replay/debug overlay, inspector, and project viewer all point at the same source-backed graph state.
3. Move commands out of the palette. Add command entrypoints through right-click, Ctrl+K, and drag-from-pin release menus. Drag-release menus must filter to compatible pin/node actions and show denied actions with exact why/fix where an existing diagnostic applies.
4. Polish node language: consistent shape/color families for exec/control/data/effect/fallible/reference pins; pin label is only the variable/field name; type appears in hover/inspector detail, not default label text.
5. Render variable/const getters as compact pure capsule/bubble nodes. Allow simple variables to embed inside field/value sockets for clean graphs, with an expand action back to a normal node.
6. Add detail toggles for types, diagnostics, effects, debug values, and package metadata so the default graph is streamlined graphite/gray rather than crowded.
7. Preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, NO_COLOR/non-visual fallbacks where terminal output is involved, and existing source transaction audit payloads.

Acceptance:
- A real Jet program opened through jet dev --target=web shows the modified hybrid Canvas UI at /canvas.
- Project/file viewer is not a command palette; commands are available through context surfaces and Ctrl+K.
- Getter capsules, embeddable variables, hover-only types, and compatible drag-from-pin menus are visible in browser proof.
- Existing graph/edit/source-control/debug features still work; no stub controls.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser proof against /canvas with console clean except known host warnings.

# Plan: jetos Studio dashboard/sidebar UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-STUDIO1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- D-JOS-STUDIO-HOST1: local projection/edit service plus browser fallback; no Canvas coupling.

Scope:
- crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/studio_projection.rs for installed app projection.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace projectional-document-first layout with a normal app shell: top status/dashboard header, left sidebar, main page, persistent staged changes footer/tray.
2. Build dashboard landing page from real data.json/source/proof facts: hosts, selected host, generation ribbon, service health, alerts, monitoring summary, proof/rollback status, and last run status. Keep copy plain and operational.
3. Build sidebar categories: Dashboard, Settings, Monitoring, Services, Packages, Secrets, Generations, Changeset, Proof/Provenance. Back categories with an internal page registry so future Studio pages register title/id/source/data needs without redesign.
4. Move settings into category pages with ordinary controls. Each setting edit must stage a source transaction and show exact Jet diff before apply.
5. Make Changeset a first-class page: unified diff, impact ledger, generation delta, proof requirements, per-hunk include where supported, Build only, Build and switch, Discard.
6. Keep one apply path. Edits from settings, dashboard alerts, rollback actions, and changeset review all stage into the same changeset/apply gate.
7. Preserve source-backed guarantees: no hidden GUI semantic state, exact config.jet diff, provenance/proof visibility, browser/headless fallback, and deterministic review output.

- jetos studio --serve opens the redesigned dashboard/sidebar UI.
- Dashboard is understandable at a glance; settings are in sidebar categories; Changeset is a sidebar page.
- A settings edit previews exact Jet diff, stages in Changeset, saves through the existing transaction service, reprojects, and can run check/plan/build/proof.

# Plan: hybrid REPL with notebook controls

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-REPL1 outcome D, with explicit owner request for notebook-style rerun/fold/unfold/pin controls.

Blocking decisions raised by this plan:

Implementation steps:
1. Preserve current REPL semantics and transcript compatibility as the floor. Non-TTY and NO_COLOR keep plain line transcripts.
2. Add turn ids to interactive TTY output. Each turn stores input, output summary, status, duration when available, folded state, pin state, and binding changes.
3. Add controls: rerun, fold, unfold, pin/unpin. Controls must have keyboard commands and textual fallbacks, not icon-only behavior.
4. Add pinned value/turn area that stays visible without changing evaluation semantics.
5. Add folded output rendering for long values/errors and unfold in place.
6. Implement docs and rerun behavior exactly per the ratified follow-up decisions.
7. Keep diagnostics verbatim; frame/styling may change, words/codes may not.

- Interactive REPL shows addressable turns with notebook controls.
- Pin/fold/unfold/rerun work in TTY mode and degrade cleanly in plain transcripts.

# Plan: jetpack/jetos hybrid CLI output

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CLI1 outcome D with owner modifications: keep colored + - ~; both -y and --yes; add nh-style dependency chain/graph visualization for long builds/downloads.

Scope:

- tests/jetpack.rs, CLI usage tests, fixture stderr/stdout snapshots where output is pinned.

Implementation steps:
1. Extend the shared Theme/Output layer with consequence-scaled rendering: quiet ledger, pinned live region for long work, plan gate for mutations, deterministic plain fallback.
2. Preserve colored +, -, ~ for plan diffs; NO_COLOR replaces color with stable text markers while keeping symbols readable.
3. Normalize confirmation bypass so -y and --yes are accepted everywhere the mutation confirmation gate appears. Non-TTY mutation without yes prints plan and exits without applying.
4. Add dependency-chain progress model for long realization/build phases: downloads, builds, cached/reused nodes, current edge, counts, size/elapsed where known. Render as a pinned graph/chain in TTY; append ledger lines in non-TTY.
5. Wire jetpack add/build/env/gc and jetos plan/build/switch/proof through the same output primitives where they already share command execution paths.
6. Erase live regions before diagnostics; diagnostics remain verbatim.
7. Keep JSON output schemas untouched unless a separate schema version decision is raised.

Acceptance:
- Trivial commands stay quiet.
- Long build/download commands show useful dependency-chain progress in TTY.
- Mutations show a plan with + - ~ and require confirmation unless -y/--yes.
- Non-TTY output is deterministic and non-interactive.

cards.title: JetOS replacement truth gate — import real NixOS and prove installed guest
cards.body: Owner asked whether JetOS can replace an entire NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager config tomorrow. Audit verdict: no. Current JetOS has substantial generation/installer/VM proof plumbing, but no full semantic NixOS/HM importer and no real installed-guest acceptance proof for the owner config. This card owns the decisions and implementation gates to make that claim true.
cards.plan:
# Plan: JetOS real NixOS replacement gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-JOS-NIXIMPORT1=C semantic NixOS/flake-parts/Home Manager importer with audited facts-only fallback.
- D-JOS-REALGUEST1=C real installed-guest proof required for replacement claims; fake QEMU only tests plumbing.
- D-JOS-DESKTOPPROOF1=C live desktop/session/app/user-home proof, not file presence.
- D-JOS-IMAGEPROOF1=C image variants are built only when bootable and smoke-proved; placeholders are staged.
- D-JOS-FIRSTBOOT1=D Studio first-boot control center with Canvas deep-link.

Implementation slices:
1. Add NixOS import IR and CLI: jet os import <flake-or-dir> --host <name> [--user <name>] [--write] [--facts-only]. Parse/evaluate available Nix facts through structured JSON, not text scraping. Generate JetOS modules for system, users, packages, services, files, secrets, overlays, specialisations, Home Manager; emit exact omissions.
2. Add fixture coverage for flake.nix, flake-parts, nixosModules, home-manager.users, overlays, mkDefault/mkForce, disabledModules, specialisations, secrets, system packages, user packages.
3. Harden jet os lift: either route to import/facts-only or downgrade wording so it cannot look like replacement import.
4. Add real-QEMU proof tier distinct from fake-tool unit tests. Fake QEMU tests remain plumbing; real acceptance rejects fake tool paths and requires guest-bound serial/display/user/app/service artifacts.
5. Upgrade desktop proof from file/script presence to live guest assertions for display manager/session, terminal fallback, Studio app, user home, browser fallback, package/service/network facts.
6. Upgrade image variants: no sparse marker says built; raw/sd/qcow only built after real artifact + smoke proof.
7. First boot: generated system launches Studio control center and proves source/proof/rollback/update health path; Canvas opens from source spans only.
8. Update docs/spec/roadmap and tests so replacement claims require import+real guest tier.

Acceptance:
- Owner-style NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager fixture imports to JetOS source with zero silent omissions.
- Generated JetOS config builds offline where fixtures provide packages, and omissions are explicit otherwise.
- Real VM tier command installs, reboots, logs in, opens Studio, proves desktop/services/packages/network/home/rollback from installed disk.
- Fake-QEMU tests cannot close #363 acceptance.

Verification:

- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack os_vm_prove

cards.title: Canvas full-language and Core parity truth gate
cards.body: Audit verdict: Canvas is source-backed for shipped graph/edit operations, but it does not fully edit every language feature, does not browse all Core methods, and the Run path is a debug-overlay simulation. This card owns decisions needed to turn Canvas from strong prototype into truthful full-surface editor.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas full-language/Core parity gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-CANVAS-PARITY1=C AST-derived semantic ratchet plus manual UX matrix.
- D-CANVAS-CORECATALOG1=C typed Core action catalog from sema-known Core facts.
- D-CANVAS-ACTIONAUTH1=C intent cards with expert authority drawers.
- D-CANVAS-CODELENS1=C explicit Edit Source mode using source transactions.
- D-CANVAS-PROOFLENS1=C proof/debug rail with stale-proof reasons.

Implementation slices:
1. Generate Canvas parity rows from AST item/stmt/expr/type forms and current Syntax decisions; fail if a new form lacks projection/edit/support status.
2. Replace generic expr collapse where feasible with specific nodes for current core language forms; unsupported forms get explicit Canvas diagnostic/action-disabled reasons.
3. Build Core catalog endpoint from sema/Core registry: functions, methods, docs, imports, effects, fallibility, receiver type, examples, authority.
4. Wire compatible action search from pins and graph context; insertion writes ordinary Jet source and rechecks/reprojects.
5. Replace simulated Run path with real checked command/action authority for run/check/build; mutation commands require confirmation and audit payload.
6. Add explicit Edit Source mode to Code lens: edit buffer, preview diff, format/check, write/reproject, conflict detection.
7. Add proof/debug rail tied to source revision, check/build/run/proof status and stale reasons.
8. Reconcile docs/spec/spec.md, docs/reference/canvas-protocol.md, and parity matrix.

Acceptance:
- Every shipped AST language form has Canvas parity status and tests or unsupported diagnostic.
- Core method browser exposes all current Core modules/methods with typed compatible insertion.
- Split/Edit Source changes text, formats/checks, reprojects graph, and can run real output.
- Canvas Run/Build authority is real, not a toast/simulation.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser smoke: edit source and graph, insert Core method, run, stale proof rail updates.
- nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-full.sh before done.

cards.title: Canvas requirement: multiple execution pins IN and OUT on nodes
cards.body: OWNER REQUIREMENT (2026-07-09, verbatim): 'multiple execution pins BOTH in and out SHOULD NOT be impossible, those are requirements for functional parity with blueprint.' Multi-exec-OUT partially exists (branch then/else, pattern arms); must generalize: any control construct with N outgoing paths projects N labeled exec outs (switch arms, loop body/done, early returns). Multi-exec-IN needs design: in Blueprint any node accepts multiple incoming exec wires (execution converges); in source-backed Jet a statement executes wherever control reaches it — N incoming exec wires = N call/reach sites of the same statement span, which today's projection renders as one exec-in accepting only one wire. Design task: projection + wiring transactions letting multiple exec sources target one node (shared continuation = e.g. moving the target into a helper fn Canvas auto-extracts, or a labeled block both paths jump to). If a canonical mechanism needs new syntax or an auto-extract convention, STOP and raise a ballot (I8: one mechanism). Deliverable: design note under docs/plans/epoch-6/ + ballot if gated + implementation with interaction scenarios (wire two exec outs into one node, assert source + execution).

cards.title: R12 parity: comptime/REPL tier-0 missing BigInt (E0956) — audit full builtin surface
cards.body:

The REPL executes through the comptime interpreter (tier-0), so every builtin the AOT backend supports but comptime doesn't is a user-visible parity break — R12 requires JIT/dev/REPL parity through the same executable TIR.

2. Audit: enumerate every builtin/Core call AOT supports vs the comptime whitelist; produce the parity matrix as a test (ui or dedicated tests/parity.rs) so new builtins can't ship AOT-only. E0956 sites are the search key.
3. Each fixed gap needs a repl transcript test; keep E0956 wording for genuinely impossible-at-comptime effects only.

log.text: Fifth repair implementation checkpoint: object-lock/root-FD model replaced by per-realization sealed private snapshot lease. Every fresh/cache result receives a lease; snapshot digest must equal canonical envelope; nested files held by inheritable exact FDs; Shell resolves executables to file FDs. Lease holds no long lock and removes snapshot on drop. JetOS copies all required bytes into generation, leaving no lease/proc symlinks; test asserts post-process generation executable remains valid. Per-object lifetime locks removed. Remaining: compile repair, reverse-order two-process proof, provider visibility lockdown, focused gates.

Fifth independent security review REJECTED 959ea91e. P1: persistent generation symlinks to /proc/self/fd dangle or retarget after lease drop; per-object lifetime locks can deadlock across opposite multi-package order; public provider trait/backends/factory still permit direct bypass; root FD does not protect nested bin/tool replacement because consumers reopen live entries; fresh realizations return lease None and remain raceable. No merge. Repair must materialize generation-private copies, eliminate/order lifetime locks, privatize raw provider surface, hand consumers exact file FDs or immutable sealed copies, and lease fresh outputs.

Scope: rotate the VAPID/JWK keypair; move secrets to an untracked file (e.g. .tower/secrets.json, gitignored) or env; keep tracked config.json non-secret; scrub or accept history exposure (owner call — repo visibility dependent). Owner-owned file: agent prepares the split + Tower code change reading the new location; owner rotates.

cards.title: Tower: archive finished board history
cards.body: tower.json is 4.2MB; 68% is closed history (496 ratified decisions = 1.7MB, 305 done cards = 1.1MB). Every write rewrites + backs up the full file (backups/ 82MB), streams it to the phone, and lands it in git (356 versions). Ballot D-TWR-ARCHIVE1 decides where finished history lives. Messages data (103KB) already removed with the messaging feature.
cards.plan:
D-TWR-ARCHIVE1=B ratified (auto-retire split live/history) MODIFIED by owner comment: keep a walk-back buffer before anything retires, and done must be strictly tested (that half lands via #463/#458). Steps:
1. store.mjs — .tower/history.json append-only ledger {decisions[], cards[], events[], each with retiredAt}. Written under the same cross-process lock; committed to git.
2. Retire policy WITH BUFFER (owner comment): on every write, retire (a) decisions status=ratified whose ratifiedAt is older than config retireAfterDays (default 3) — inside the window they stay in tower.json, show in the UI 'recently decided' strip, and tower decision reopen works one-step; (b) cards phase=done older than the same buffer AND passing the #463 done-gate rules; their questions ride along; (c) events beyond the newest 500.
3. Walk-back UX: Now view gets a collapsed 'Recently decided (N) — reversible for X days' strip listing buffered ratifications with one-tap Reopen. Reopen pulls it back to open and reverts the card advance.
4. Merged reads: findCard/decision show/card show fall through to history transparently; tower archive restore <id> moves an item back to live (reopen for ratified decisions). Board Done counts read a per-epoch summary; full done lists lazy-load via GET /api/history?epoch=.
5. CLI: tower archive status|show <id>|restore <id>. First write after upgrade migrates the existing 496 ratified decisions + 305 done cards (all outside any buffer) → tower.json ~0.5MB.
6. Tests: buffer respected (nothing retires early), reopen-from-buffer, retire-after-buffer, merged reads, restore, migration on a live-shaped fixture, backups shrink.
7. Docs: Tower README/AGENTS.md + tower-setup skill (retireAfterDays).
Exit: tower.json ≤ ~0.6MB after migration; every retired item still reachable by id; a ratification can be walked back within the buffer from phone UI; suite green.

log.text: D-TWR-ARCHIVE1=B ratified with comment. Plan honors both comment clauses: retire buffer w/ one-tap walk-back (steps 2-3); stricter done testing enforced by #463/#458 (linked). Ready to implement after #463 lands the done-gate it references.
Activated into sidequest track

cards.title: Tower: one-shot agent work packet
cards.body: Starting a card today takes 5 CLI reads and still misses ratification comments / open questions buried in JSON — the top cause of bounced cards. Ballot D-TWR-BRIEF1 decides the agent-facing surface: brief command vs rendered brief file vs MCP tools.
cards.plan:
D-TWR-BRIEF1=A ratified — one-shot work packet. Consolidates the brief half of #457 (that card narrows to lint; this card owns brief). Steps:
1. CLI: tower brief [#N] [--agent me] [--json] [--no-claim]. No ref → pick via nextCards (workOrder order); claims for --agent unless --no-claim; already-claimed → error naming holder.
2. Packet contents (nothing an agent must fetch elsewhere): card num/title/body/plan/phase/priority/workOrder; blockedBy with live blocker state; epoch + milestone (goal, criteria); card criteria[] state once #463 lands; every linked decision VERBATIM from live store — status, outcome, and the owner's ratification comment in full (kills the paraphrase-stale-ballot failure); open questions; refs[] — new optional card field of doc paths, plus paths auto-harvested from body/plan; 5-line rules footer (--by required, phase honesty, verify≠builder, expect-rev, handoff on release).
3. HTTP GET /api/brief?card=&agent= returning the same JSON.
4. Human render ≤ one screen; --json stable schema (documented in AGENTS.md API table).
5. Tests: packet completeness incl. ratification comment (regression), claim/--no-claim/claimed-by-other, refs harvest, json schema snapshot.
6. Docs/skills: tower skill session loop step 2 becomes 'tower brief'; Tower/AGENTS.md; sub-agent brief pattern = literally `tower brief '#N' --agent <me>`.
Exit (from #457, kept): brief output is sufficient to work a real card with no other reads — validated by running one card end-to-end from the packet alone; suite green.

log.text: D-TWR-BRIEF1=A ratified. Plan written; brief scope consolidated here from #457 (which narrows to tower lint + next --burndown). Ready to implement; criteria block in packet activates when #463 lands.
Activated into sidequest track

cards.title: Tower: exit criteria that gate done
cards.body: Cards have bounced (e.g. #360 twice) because done was claimable by assertion: exit criteria live in prose and nothing mechanical checks them, and owner acceptance verdicts ended up in card logs. Ballot D-TWR-CRIT1 decides the enforcement model (machine-checked criteria / acceptance ballots / hybrid flag).
cards.plan:
D-TWR-CRIT1=C ratified — criteria list enforced everywhere + acceptance ballots on flagged cards. Steps:
1. store.mjs — card.criteria[]: {n, text, status open|met|verified, metBy, verifiedBy, evidence, at}. addCard/updateCard accept criteria; new mutations addCriterion/meetCriterion/verifyCriterion. Validation: verify rejected when verifiedBy === metBy or === assignee at meet time (E_CRITERIA_SELF).
2. Done-gate (agent-hard, owner-soft per D-TWRGUARD1=C): updateCard to phase done with --by ≠ owner rejected (E_CRITERIA) while any criterion unverified — only for cards that HAVE criteria (legacy cards unaffected). Owner writes bypass.
3. card.needsAcceptance flag (set at greenlight or any time by owner). On agent done-attempt with all criteria verified: auto-mint decision D-ACCEPT-<num> (options accept/bounce, body = per-criterion evidence summary), card stays verify; done only when owner ratifies accept; bounce comment reopens to building + log.
4. CLI: tower card criteria '#N' --add "…" | --meet n --evidence "…" --by X | --verify n --evidence "…" --by Y. tower brief (#462) includes criteria state.
5. UI: checklist w/ per-item state + evidence in card modal; acceptance ballots render in Now focus mode like any decision.
6. Tests (Tower/test): gate refusal, verifier≠builder, owner bypass, flag→mint→accept, flag→mint→bounce-reopen, legacy cards unaffected.
7. Docs: Tower/AGENTS.md, README, tower + tower-ballot skills.
Exit: all listed tests green; #458 gates can consume criteria[]; a flagged card demonstrably cannot reach done without an owner accept.

log.text: D-TWR-CRIT1=C ratified. Plan written; also carries D-TWR-ARCHIVE1 comment 'enforce stricter done testing' — this card is that enforcement. Ready to implement.
Activated into sidequest track

cards.title: Tower: Board view for 434 cards
cards.body: With Agents removed the UI is Now + Board. Board is an accordion wall that answers neither burndown-at-a-glance nor find-fast on phone. Ballot D-TWR-BOARD1 picks the Board archetype (roadmap ledger / ops table / spotlight search). Follow-up candidate once decided: in-app viewer for docs/plans+proposals (the old tools/Tower app had one).
cards.plan:
D-TWR-BOARD1=A ratified with comment: ADD a NEW page prototyping a hybrid of A (roadmap ledger) & B (ops table); DO NOT replace or change the current Board. Steps:
1. New third tab 'Radar' (Now · Board · Radar; keyboard 3, ⌘K entry). Board view code untouched — zero diffs to viewBoard.
2. Radar layout per epoch (active epochs only, current first): header row = name + progress bar + 30-day burndown sparkline (computed from events: card.update transitions to done, bucketed per day) + active/done counts; milestone bars with met/total and a stall badge when no progress event for 5+ days.
3. Under each epoch header: the B half — dense sortable table of that epoch's ACTIVE cards (num, title, lane, priority, order, assignee, updated-age). Column-header sort; type-to-filter box; inline edits for lane-safe fields (priority, workOrder, assignee) via existing card/update API; row click opens the normal card modal.
4. Done/frozen never render on Radar; per-epoch 'ledger' link shows done list (from tower.json now; switches to GET /api/history when #461 lands — soft dependency, not blocking).
5. Server: burndown series computed in project() (store-side helper + unit test) so the client stays dumb.
6. Tests: burndown/stall helper unit tests in Tower/test; existing suite green.
7. Acceptance (owner comment = this is a prototype he wants to SEE): card flagged for owner acceptance — demo on his phone + desktop, he compares against untouched Board, then decides keep/iterate/drop via the acceptance ballot. Frontend acceptance = feature-by-feature vs this plan in his real browser, not pty tests.
Exit: Radar renders live board data with burndown + table hybrid; Board byte-identical in behavior; owner acceptance ballot answered.

log.text: D-TWR-BOARD1=A ratified with comment honored verbatim: new Radar tab prototypes the A+B hybrid, current Board untouched, owner reviews prototype before anything replaces anything. Ready to implement.

decisions.title: Inside `.{ }` / `T.{ }` literals, adopt Zig-style `.field = val` member syntax to enable LSP dot-completion?
decisions.gist: D-DOTCTOR1/2 (ratified 2026-06-25) established `T.{ }` and `.{ }` as the struct literal spellings with `field: val` syntax. This card reopens only the inside-the-braces field syntax: should fields use a leading dot (`.field = val`) to enable LSP completion when the user types `.`, or stay with the current `field: val` colon style?
decisions.explainer: D-DOTCTOR1=A (ratified, not yet implemented) uses `field: val` inside braces, matching named-parameter and record-update patterns elsewhere. Changing to `.field = val` would require a different tokenization rule inside literal braces (dot-name-equals vs name-colon) and amend D-DOTCTOR1. The LSP motivation is real: when a user types `.` inside `T.{ }`, completion engines can offer field names. However, LSP can also complete after the bare `field` token using the expected type from context — the leading dot is not strictly required for completion. Adding `.field =` also introduces a third sigil family inside braces. I8: if `field: val` and `.field = val` coexist, that is two ways to mean the same thing — reject unless one fully replaces the other.
decisions.story: I type `Server.{` and then `.` and the IDE shows me exactly which fields are available. It feels like autocomplete in a GUI form — the dot is the trigger that says 'I want a field name here'.

options.name: Keep `field: val` (status quo, D-DOTCTOR1=A)
options.detail: The ratified spelling stands. LSP completion is implemented in the server using the expected type from context — no dot trigger needed. Consistent with named-parameter syntax elsewhere. No I8 issue. Recommend.

options.name: Adopt `.field = val` Zig-style, replace `field: val` in literals
options.detail: Amend D-DOTCTOR1 so struct literal fields use `.name = value`. The leading dot is a uniform trigger inside any `{ }` context (struct literal vs block) that LSP and parsers can key on. Creates a syntactic split: `fn foo(field: val)` named args use colon, struct literals use `.field =`. Introduces inconsistency across two very similar contexts.

options.name: Allow both (reject — I8 violation)
options.detail: Permit either `field: val` or `.field = val` inside literals. Violates I8 — two spellings for one job. Beginners will encounter both in real code and wonder which is right. Reject.

comparisons.note: Zig uses `.field = value` inside struct literals, enabling dot-completion and distinguishing member names from locals.
Zig uses `.field = value` inside struct literals uniformly. The leading dot is the LSP completion trigger and creates a consistent rule: dot-anything inside braces is a field init.
Rust struct literals use bare `field: value` with no leading sigil. IDEs complete field names from the struct definition without needing a dot trigger.

decisions.bestCurrent: Zig: Zig uses `.field = value` inside struct literals, enabling dot-completion and distinguishing member names from locals.
decisions.recommendation: Keep `field: value`: Jet already uses `:` for named association across fields, args, maps, and types. Zig wins completion, but Jet wins one-path consistency; LSP can still complete from expected type.

decisions.title: Add a blessed core library type for loading/pending/unknown async states, or leave to user enums?
decisions.gist: Async UIs often need a four-state value: not-asked, loading, ok(T), error(E). Jet has `T?` (optional) and `T ? E` (fallible). Should Jet add a blessed `Loadable<T>` or `AsyncState<T, E>` enum in the stdlib, or leave this pattern to user-defined enums?
decisions.explainer: The four-state pattern is already expressible today with a user enum and a `match`. Adding a blessed type risks I8: it's a second optional-like container alongside `T?` and `T ? E`. A stdlib enum (B) is lower cost than a language keyword (C) and avoids I1/I8 issues, but it still adds surface area to the beginner namespace. The case for it is that UI/reactive code is a target domain (replace-Swift lens) and the pattern is ubiquitous enough to warrant a canonical name. The case against: one extra enum is not a hardship, and a blessed type could fragment — `Loadable` in one codebase, user enum in another, both in the stdlib docs.
decisions.story: Every screen in my app has a data-fetch lifecycle: not loaded yet, loading spinner, loaded data, error banner. I want a type that models this cleanly without me defining the same four-variant enum in every project.

options.name: Leave to user enums (status quo)
options.detail: No new stdlib type. The pattern is one enum away. Documentation in the cookbook shows the canonical four-variant shape so every project lands on the same idiom. Keeps surface small (I8). The reactive library (D-REACT1) can export its own `Signal<T>` without a generic Loadable. Recommend.

options.name: Ship a blessed `Loadable<T, E>` stdlib enum
options.detail: Add `core.async.Loadable<T, E>` (or `core.ui.AsyncState`) to the stdlib with variants Idle / Loading / Loaded(T) / Failed(E). Consistent naming across all Jet projects. Cost: adds a type to learn, risks being wrong for some use cases (no Idle? two error types?), and may become the 'official' way even when a user enum is clearer.

options.name: Language-level pending state / keyword
options.detail: Make `pending` a first-class language concept: `T | pending` or a `?~` suffix. Deep integration — the compiler knows what 'pending' means, enabling flow-sensitivity. Very high cost, hard to reverse, I8 concern (third optional-like mechanism), and the motivating UI use cases don't require language-level semantics. Reject.

comparisons.note: Elm has no stdlib Loadable; the community converged on a `RemoteData` package with four variants (NotAsked / Loading / Failure e / Success a). A library, not a language feature.
comparisons.code:
type RemoteData e a
    = NotAsked
    | Loading
    | Failure e
    | Success a

comparisons.note: Swift has no canonical async-state type. Every team defines their own. The fragmentation pain is real — it's one argument for a blessed stdlib enum.

decisions.title: Should Jet codify a written core library ergonomic-laws checklist?
decisions.gist: The deeper question is not whether to write a doc — it is what enforcement mechanism Jet's rubric uses. Written guidelines enforced by PR review is the Rust model; it is explicitly weaker than what Jet already achieves (type-by-construction per D-DBDRIVER1, namespace separation per D-RANDSPLIT1). Jet's answer should be mechanical: encode each ergonomic law as a named lint, make the lint the source of truth, and generate the doc from it. A pure doc-checklist reviewed by humans is one pressure-filled review away from being ceremonial.
decisions.explainer: The checklist would live in docs/ (not the spec) and be referenced in PR review. It codifies things we already believe — like 'make misuse a type error', 'never accept raw strings where a path object works', 'CSPRNG and PRNG must not share a namespace' — so reviewers have a checklist rather than relying on institutional memory. It has no syntax impact and no I8 risk. It does require someone to author and maintain it; the risk is it becomes stale or ceremonial. This is a process/docs decision, not a language feature.
decisions.story: I keep catching the same API shape mistakes in review — raw strings instead of typed path objects, functions that are easy to call wrong. I want a short checklist I can point to instead of re-litigating the same principles every time.
decisions.detail: Adversarial pass (2026-06-28): (1) Option A as written is the Rust social-convention model, not the Jet structural-safety model — add rule taxonomy and lint-graduation plan or it will calcify. (2) D-RINGLAYER1 (open) makes any "valid core library API" rubric incomplete until ring layering is decided; reserve a ring-placement section. (3) Option C (lints-first) is the stronger Jet-native answer: encode each rule as a named jet-lint, generate the doc from lint annotations so it cannot go stale — and closes the ecosystem coverage gap since lints apply to jetpack packages too. (4) Option D needs a concrete trigger condition (D-RINGLAYER1 ratified + D-IFC1 ratified + 20 Core APIs across 3 domains) rather than a vague epoch reference.

options.name: Lints-first: named jet-lints, doc generated from annotations (recommended)
options.detail: Encode each ergonomic law as a named compiler lint (e.g. `jet::core::stringly-typed-arg`, `jet::core::csprng-namespace-leak`). The rubric doc is auto-generated from lint metadata — name, why-clause, fix suggestion — so it cannot go stale. CI runs the lint set on every core library addition as a required gate; lints are optionally enabled for jetpack packages ecosystem-wide. Start with 5 high-value lints covering patterns already surfaced by prior decisions. Ring-placement rules become ring-qualified lint attributes once D-RINGLAYER1 is ratified; no prose reserve section needed. This is I8-clean: one mechanical path, not a social-convention document.

options.name: Author a tiered rubric doc (no lint generation)
options.detail: Write a ~10-rule doc in docs/ classifying rules as compiler-enforced, lint-tracked, or convention. Human-reviewed in PR. Weaker than A: doc can go stale, enforcement is social, ring-placement and taint-sink rules cannot be added until D-RINGLAYER1/D-IFC1 settle.

options.name: Defer — capture emerging patterns as one-off lint proposals until Epoch 6
options.detail: No rubric now. File individual lint proposals as patterns surface; revisit a unified rubric in Epoch 6 when D-RINGLAYER1, D-IFC1, and 20+ Core APIs across 3 domains are stable. Until then, institutional knowledge lives in PR comments and individual lint PRs.
options.code:
// No rubric doc; defer to Epoch 6
// Pattern surfaced → file lint proposal → implement if approved

comparisons.note: Rust API Guidelines codify naming, ownership, error, and trait conventions so std/crates feel coherent across teams.

Rust has a published API guidelines doc (rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines) that is explicitly required for std contributions. It catches naming, error handling, and ergonomics issues before they land.
Swift has a mandatory API design guidelines doc. Every new core library addition is checked against it, enforcing naming clarity and call-site readability.
comparisons.code:
// Swift guideline: "Prefer method and function names that make use sites form grammatical English phrases"
array.insert(x, at: i)   // not array.insert(i, x)

decisions.bestCurrent: Rust: Rust API Guidelines codify naming, ownership, error, and trait conventions so std/crates feel coherent across teams.
decisions.recommendation: Encode each ergonomic rule as a named jet-lint; generate the rubric doc from lint annotations so it cannot go stale (Option A). Ecosystem-wide: lints apply to both core library and jetpack packages.
